item.title: Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations.
item.dc:creator: Guo QJ, Liu Q, Bossi P, Bonomo P, Colevas AD, Lee NY, Lu TZ, Lee V, Mehanna H, Ng WT, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Guo QJ, Liu Q, Bossi P, Bonomo P, Colevas AD, Lee NY, Lu TZ, Lee V, Mehanna H, Ng WT, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00347-5
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42933448



Abstract:
Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). We recommend that curative-intent treatment should be offered to medically fit patients with no more than three metastatic lesions in two or fewer organs at baseline or following response to systemic therapy; multimodality treatment (comprising immunochemotherapy, locoregional radiotherapy, metastasis-directed therapy, and maintenance therapy) is recommended. This guideline provides a practical framework for standardisation of clinical management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma and identification of key evidence gaps for future research.

item.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
item.dc:creator: Tao K, Lin Z, Zhang P, Chi P, Xiao Y, Hou Z, Xu X, Zhang A, Qiu X, Wu J, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Tao K, Lin Z, Zhang P, Chi P, Xiao Y, Hou Z, Xu X, Zhang A, Qiu X, Wu J, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00446-8
Published: 2026-Nov-01
PMID: 42927765



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival. METHODS: This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting. FINDINGS: Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group. INTERPRETATION: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted. item.title: Response-Adapted Surgery Following Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Oral Cavity Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An Era-Based Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.dc:creator: Rai S, Agarwal M, Singh A, Singh P, Bansal K, Karthik P, Gugliani A, Garg N, Leela P, Tandon S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Rai S, Agarwal M, Singh A, Singh P, Bansal K, Karthik P, Gugliani A, Garg N, Leela P, Tandon S, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70532
Published: 2026-Oct-29
PMID: 42952328



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Evidence regarding response-adapted resection after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma remains limited. METHODS: We compared conventional-era (2018-2021) and response-adapted-era (2022-2024) surgery after NACT. Margins, recurrence, 2-year survival, and surgical outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: Among 129 patients (58 conventional; 71 response-adapted), positive margins occurred in 3.4% versus 1.4% and local recurrence in 12.1% versus 7.0%. Two-year disease-free survival (DFS) was 56.6% versus 67.8% (log-rank p = 0.135). Adjusted DFS HR for the response-adapted era was 0.54 (95% CI 0.28-1.04; p = 0.066). ENE predicted inferior DFS (HR 3.60; p < 0.001). Responder-only analysis showed no significant survival difference. CONCLUSIONS: No observed increase in positive margins or local recurrence accompanied the later surgical strategy. Retrospective selection, unequal follow-up, and limited events preclude conclusions of noninferiority or a causal survival benefit.

item.title: Treatment Outcomes in Osteosarcoma of the Head and Neck: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.dc:creator: Magri A, Quaiattini A, Mlynarek A, Richardson K, Hier M, Sadeghi N, Saleh R, Aoude A, Sultanem K, Di Maio S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Magri A, Quaiattini A, Mlynarek A, Richardson K, Hier M, Sadeghi N, Saleh R, Aoude A, Sultanem K, Di Maio S, et al.
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70452
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42952222



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head and neck osteosarcomas (HNOS) are rare, accounting for ~1% of head and neck malignancies. This study systematically evaluated the role of chemotherapy (CT) and radiotherapy (RT) on survival outcomes. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were performed following PRISMA guidelines across six databases. Treatment arms included surgery alone or combined with CT and/or RT, given in neoadjuvant or adjuvant settings. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). RESULTS: Thirty-one studies comprising 2006 patients were included. Jaw tumors had superior OS compared to skull base tumors. CT significantly improved OS (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.89) and DFS (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.98), particularly in the neoadjuvant setting, whereas RT showed no survival benefit. CONCLUSIONS: Systemic therapy in combination with surgery improves OS and DFS in HNOS, reinforcing its importance as part of curative-intent treatment.

item.title: Patient reported swallowing outcomes after prophylactic versus reactive gastrostomy during chemoradiotherapy for head and neck cancer: Results from the SwallPEG randomized trial.
item.dc:creator: Dragan T, Duprez F, Digonnet A, Mootassim-Billah S, Gossum AV, Lalami Y, Vakaet V, Salmon M, Paesmans M, Gestel DV
item.description:
Authors: Dragan T, Duprez F, Digonnet A, Mootassim-Billah S, Gossum AV, Lalami Y, Vakaet V, Salmon M, Paesmans M, Gestel DV
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111835
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42951256



Abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare prophylactic (p-) versus reactive (r-) percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) placement during definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for locally advanced, nonmetastatic head and neck carcinoma, with swallowing-related quality of life (QoL) as the primary endpoint. MATERIALS AND METHODS: SwallPEG is a prospective, multicenter, randomized phase III trial of patients undergoing definitive cisplatin-based CRT. Patients were randomized 1:1 to pPEG before CRT or rPEG based on predefined nutritional criteria. All received standardized nutritional counseling, weekly dietitian assessment, and swallowing rehabilitation. The primary endpoint was swallowing-related QoL at 6 months, assessed using the MD Anderson Dysphagia Inventory (MDADI) composite score. Secondary endpoints included nutritional outcomes, treatment-related toxicity, PEG-related complications, and early oncologic outcomes. RESULTS: Fifty-seven patients were analyzed (pPEG, n = 28; rPEG, n = 29). Following a prespecified interim analysis that reached the futility boundary, the trial was closed early in the context of slow accrual. Median MDADI composite scores at 6 months were 69.5 (Q1-Q3, 60.0-80.0) and 74.7 (Q1-Q3, 58.9-87.9), respectively (P = 0.595). Swallowing function declined during CRT and subsequently recovered without a significant between-group difference. Weight loss at 6 months was comparable (-7.0 % vs - 9.0 %; P = 0.67). No significant differences were observed in treatment-related toxicity, PEG-related complications, chemotherapy delivery, or early oncologic outcomes. CONCLUSION: No difference in swallowing-related QoL was demonstrated between (p-) and rPEG strategies. Although interpretation is limited by early trial closure and reduced sample size, the findings support individualized PEG placement based on clinical need.

item.title: Multilevel factors associated with human papillomavirus vaccination coverage in Iowa youth: Evidence from a statewide immunization registry.
item.dc:creator: Hill A, Carrel M, Vu M, Zahnd WE, Janio E, Brandt HM, Sukalski J, Kahl AR, Gufue ZH, Askelson NM
item.description:
Authors: Hill A, Carrel M, Vu M, Zahnd WE, Janio E, Brandt HM, Sukalski J, Kahl AR, Gufue ZH, Askelson NM
Journal: Preventive medicine | DOI: 10.1016/j.ypmed.2026.108691
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42951083



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination at the earliest opportunity is critical for preventing cervical, vulvar, vaginal, anal, rectal, and oropharyngeal cancers. This study examined individual-level and area-level factors associated with HPV vaccination among Iowa youth. METHODS: We analyzed Iowa Immunization Registry Information System data for youth aged 9-17 years, linked to ZIP Code Tabulation Area socioeconomic and demographic measures. Hierarchical Bayesian spatial models estimated HPV vaccination initiation, completion at any age, and on-time completion. RESULTS: Receipt of school-required and other routinely recommended vaccines was strongly associated with HPV vaccination. Compared with youth who received both vaccine types, those who received only school-required vaccines or only other routinely recommended vaccines had lower HPV vaccination odds (ORs = 0.01-0.42, 95% CrIs = [0.01, 0.43]). Female youth, insured youth, and those of Hispanic or Latino ethnicity had higher vaccination odds. Youth in rural, small town, and micropolitan areas had lower odds than those in metropolitan areas (ORs = 0.89-0.93, 95% CrIs = [0.85, 0.97]). Area-level education, housing, and local HPV vaccination rates were associated with vaccination. CONCLUSIONS: Individual-level and area-level characteristics were associated with HPV vaccination. Interventions promoting preventive care and routine youth vaccination while addressing geographic disparities may improve vaccine coverage and reduce HPV-related cancer risk.

item.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant (castration-resistant) prostate cancer (TALAPRO-2): a biomarker analysis of circulating tumour DNA and cells for prognosis and molecular profiling.
item.dc:creator: Yip SM, Laird AD, Agarwal N, Zschäbitz S, Fizazi K, Matsubara N, Joung JY, Karsh LI, Carles J, Fay AP, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Yip SM, Laird AD, Agarwal N, Zschäbitz S, Fizazi K, Matsubara N, Joung JY, Karsh LI, Carles J, Fay AP, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00355-4
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42950862



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The TALAPRO-2 trial showed improved radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival with first-line talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (APMR; also referred to as castration-resistant prostate cancer) unselected for homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations treated. We aimed to assess HRR gene alteration status agreement between prospective solid tumour tissue and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) testing, the potential complementary value of prospective and retrospective ctDNA testing, and the prognostic utility of baseline ctDNA burden, changes in ctDNA burden, and circulating tumour cell (CTC) reductions. METHODS: In TALAPRO-2, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, men aged 18 years or older (≥20 years in Japan) with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic metastatic APMR prostate cancer and no previous life-prolonging systemic therapy for APMR disease were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive once daily, oral talazoparib 0·5 mg plus enzalutamide 160 mg or placebo plus enzalutamide and stratified by HRR gene alteration status and previous treatment for androgen pathway modulator-naive/sensitive disease. The sponsor, patients, and investigators were masked to allocation of talazoparib or placebo; enzalutamide was open label. In this exploratory analysis, HRR gene alteration status agreement was evaluated in the unselected intention-to-treat cohort between solid tumour tissue prospectively tested using a clinical trial assay based on FoundationOne CDx and retrospectively tested ctDNA samples, collected at screening and assessed using an assay based on FoundationOne Liquid CDx. Tumour burden was categorised as positive or negative (ctDNA tumour fraction detectable or not detectable). Reductions in CTCs, enumerated using CELLSEARCH, were defined as conversion (from five or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to four or fewer cells per 7·5 mL of blood) or CTC0 (from one or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to zero). Radiographic progression-free survival was assessed for patients with baseline ctDNA positivity (positive vs negative) and for patients with ctDNA conversion and CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 (and week 17 for CTC conversion and CTC0) by treatment group. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrial.gov, NCT03395197 and is active, not recruiting. FINDINGS: Between Jan 7, 2019, and Sept 17, 2020, 805 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned (402 to talazoparib plus enzalutamide; 403 to placebo plus enzalutamide); median follow-up for radiographic progression-free survival was 24·9 months (IQR 21·9-30·2) for the talazoparib group and 24·6 months (14·4-30·2) for the placebo group. A high concordance in HRR gene alteration status was observed between results from prospectively tested solid tumour tissue samples and retrospectively tested screening ctDNA samples (reported for 739 [92%] of 805 enrolled patients), with 84% (421 of 501) agreement in patients evaluable as either HRR-deficient or HRR-non-deficient by both tests. Median radiographic progression-free survival for positive versus negative ctDNA burden was 21·0 months (95% CI 16·5-not reached [NR]) versus NR (NR-NR), respectively (hazard ratio [HR] 2·46; 95% CI 1·68-3·60; p<0·0001) with talazoparib plus enzalutamide, and 11·0 months (8·4-13·8) versus 33·2 months (30·3-NR), respectively (HR 4·03; 2·85-5·72; p<0·0001) with placebo plus enzalutamide. In both groups, week 9 conversion from positive to negative ctDNA was prognostic of improved radiographic progression-free survival versus remaining ctDNA positive. Patients remaining ctDNA negative had more favourable radiographic progression-free survival versus conversion from positive to negative ctDNA. CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 were prognostic for radiographic progression-free survival benefit in both groups. INTERPRETATION: Our results support broad prognostic utility of ctDNA burden and CTC enumeration in metastatic APMR prostate cancer, including in the context of poly(ADP) ribose polymerase inhibitor therapy. FUNDING: Pfizer.

item.title: Darovasertib and Crizotinib First-Line Treatment for Metastatic Uveal Melanoma: Overall Survival, Efficacy, and Safety From the OptimUM-01 Study.
item.dc:creator: McKean M, Chmielowski B, Butler MO, Carvajal RD, Rodon J, Carlino MS, Kim KB, Wise-Draper TM, Khan S, Salama AKS, et al.
item.description:
Authors: McKean M, Chmielowski B, Butler MO, Carvajal RD, Rodon J, Carlino MS, Kim KB, Wise-Draper TM, Khan S, Salama AKS, et al.
Journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology | DOI: 10.1200/JCO-26-00802
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42950186



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM) has poor prognosis with limited therapies. GNAQ/11 mutations that activate protein kinase C (PKC) are detected in 95% of UM tumors. Darovasertib is a first-in-class, oral, targeted PKC inhibitor that, in combination with the MET inhibitor crizotinib, has shown responses and encouraging survival outcomes in early mUM clinical trials. Here, we present phase 2 results in first-line patients with mUM treated with darovasertib 300 mg twice a day and crizotinib 200 mg twice a day. METHODS: The OptimUM-01 study was a phase I/II, multicenter, open-label, dose escalation and expansion study of darovasertib in patients with solid tumors harboring GNAQ/11 mutations irrespective of human leukocyte antigen status; this analysis focuses on the phase II expansion in previously untreated patients with mUM. Eligibility criteria included Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors v1.1 measurable disease, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1, and adequate organ function. Study end points included safety, objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DOR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). RESULTS: Overall, 44 treatment-naïve patients were enrolled. The most common adverse events (AEs) were diarrhea (95.2%), nausea (84.1%), peripheral edema (61.4%), and vomiting (52.3%). The most common grade 3 or greater AEs were pulmonary embolism (9.1%) and iron deficiency anemia (6.8%). AEs leading to discontinuation occurred in three patients (6.8%). ORR was 34.1%, DOR was 9.0 months, and DCR was 90.2% at 8 weeks. The median PFS and OS were 7.0 months (95% CI, 5.0 to 8.3) and 21.1 months (95% CI, 11.9 to 20.7), respectively. CONCLUSION: Results from OptimUM-01 suggest that the combination of darovasertib and crizotinib has encouraging efficacy with a manageable safety profile and may represent a first-in-class targeted treatment option for patients with previously untreated mUM.

item.title: Multimedia versus audio-based education for improving dentists' nutrition-related knowledge and behavior: A randomized comparative study.
item.dc:creator: Farhadi M, Pakdaman A, Gholami M
item.description:
Authors: Farhadi M, Pakdaman A, Gholami M
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360426
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42949884



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nutrition plays a crucial role in oral health, influencing the risk of caries, periodontal disease, erosion, and oral cancers. Dentists are key providers of dietary guidance, but require adequate knowledge to do this effectively. This study compared the impact of multimedia versus audio-based educational interventions on the knowledge and self-reported behavior of general dentists in Tehran regarding nutrition and oral health. METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 166 general dentists in Tehran were recruited in 2023 through professional online platforms and randomly allocated to either a multimedia-based or an audio-based educational intervention. Knowledge (11 items) and behavior (9 items) regarding the impact of nutrition on periodontal health, dental caries, oral cancer, and erosion were assessed using a validated questionnaire. The educational intervention was delivered over a one-month period. Within-group changes were assessed using paired t-tests, between-group differences using repeated-measures ANOVA, and the effect of demographic variables on post-intervention scores using ANCOVA, with baseline values as covariates (α = 0.05). RESULTS: Of the participants, 53.6% were women, and 37.9% worked in private practice. Both groups demonstrated significant improvements in knowledge and behavior scores following the intervention (p < 0.001), with greater gains observed in the multimedia group. Analysis of covariance indicated that baseline knowledge and behavior were not significantly associated with age, gender, dental school, years of professional experience, or practice setting. CONCLUSION: Both multimedia- and audio-based educational interventions effectively improved dentists' knowledge and self-reported behaviors related to nutrition and oral health. Therefore, given dentists' busy work schedules, the use of these educational approaches may enhance their capacity to provide evidence-based counseling in the field of nutrition and oral health.

item.title: Microbiome plasticity during the early life-stage of the angelshark (Squatina squatina) in Las Teresitas (Canary Islands).
item.dc:creator: Bañeras T, Jiménez-Alvarado D, Toledo-Padilla H, Camps-Lahora L, Castro JJ, Espino-Ruano A, Guerra-Marrero A, Couce-Montero L, Meyers EKM, Bañeras L
item.description:
Authors: Bañeras T, Jiménez-Alvarado D, Toledo-Padilla H, Camps-Lahora L, Castro JJ, Espino-Ruano A, Guerra-Marrero A, Couce-Montero L, Meyers EKM, Bañeras L
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361287
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42949873



Abstract:
Shark microbiome studies offer acute insights into host health, immunity, and ecological interactions, yet remain poorly studied compared to other marine vertebrates. Shark-associated microbial communities, despite being species-specific, are influenced by environmental conditions and feeding ecology. In this study, we aimed to characterize shifts in the microbiome of the Critically Endangered angelshark (Squatina squatina) during the early stages of development and to assess how environmental factors contribute to the shaping of a specific microbiota. Samples from thirty-nine juvenile angelsharks were collected from Las Teresitas nursery area in the Canary Islands over one year. Skin, oral and cloacal microbiomes were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. The sizes of individuals ranged between 24 and 42 cm in length. The shark microbiome was clearly distinct from the surrounding environment, indicating a unique composition from early life stages. Dominant bacteria present in the shark microbiomes included Vibrionaceae (up to 96%), Pseudoalteromonas (up to 63%), Rhodobacteraceae (up to 57%) and Alteromonadaceae (up to 20%). Seawater had a greater influence than sediment on the external skin microbiome, especially in younger individuals. This was not expected due to the burial behaviour of the species. Notably, the abundance of Pseudoalteromonadaceae (assessed by qPCR) was positively correlated with shark growth but was independent of the skin mucus. This suggests a protective role of this phylotype in younger individuals and may help in the adaptation to habitat conditions. This is the first comprehensive microbiome study in angelsharks, highlighting the importance of environmental preservation for microbial integrity and juvenile fitness.

item.title: Evolving Cancer Survival in Taiwan Over 25 Years: Nowcasting with the Survivorship-Period-Cohort Model.
item.dc:creator: Chiang CJ, Tsai DR, Yang YW, Lin LJ, Lai MC, Lee WC
item.description:
Authors: Chiang CJ, Tsai DR, Yang YW, Lin LJ, Lai MC, Lee WC
Journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology | DOI: 10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-26-1180
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42949761



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer has been the leading cause of death in Taiwan since 1982, but long-term survival trends remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated 25-year cancer survival trends, including stage-specific outcomes. METHODS: We analyzed Taiwan Cancer Registry data for patients aged 15-99 years diagnosed with cancer between 1996 and 2021. We estimated the cancer survival index for all sites combined and age- and sex-adjusted 5-year relative survival ratios for individual cancers. The Ederer II cohort method was used for diagnoses before 2018, and the survivorship-period-cohort model was used to nowcast survival for diagnoses in 2018-2020. TNM stage-specific survival was evaluated for 17 cancers diagnosed during 2010-2017. RESULTS: The 5-year cancer survival index increased from 46.8% in 1996 to a nowcast estimate of 56.2% in 2020. Survival improved most for small intestine, lung, and nasopharyngeal cancers, with lung adenocarcinoma also shifting toward earlier-stage diagnosis. Survival declined for cervical, renal pelvis, bladder, brain and CNS, and gallbladder cancers. Stage-specific survival remained largely stable for most cancers, whereas lung cancer showed clear gains, including across all stages of adenocarcinoma and in late-stage squamous cell carcinoma. CONCLUSIONS: Nationwide cancer survival improved substantially, but persistent cancer-specific gaps highlight priorities for early detection, treatment, and cancer control. IMPACT: These population-based estimates provide timely evidence for monitoring cancer prognosis, evaluating cancer-control progress, and identifying cancers and stages requiring greater clinical and public health attention.

item.title: Preoperative Iron and Blood Transfusions in Head and Neck Free Flap Reconstruction: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.dc:creator: Levy BB, Pradhan A, Choudhary L, Podolsky EJ, Noel CW, de Almeida JR, Goldstein DP, Gilbert RW, Irish JC, Brown DH, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Levy BB, Pradhan A, Choudhary L, Podolsky EJ, Noel CW, de Almeida JR, Goldstein DP, Gilbert RW, Irish JC, Brown DH, et al.
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70492
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42949235



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether preoperative intravenous iron infusion is associated with reduced postoperative packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion risk and transfusion volume among patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Tertiary head and neck cancer centre. METHODS: Adult patients undergoing free flap reconstruction for head and neck cancer between January 2022 and May 2025 were included. Starting June 2022, patients with baseline hemoglobin <130 g/L underwent routine preoperative transferrin saturation testing. Patients with transferrin saturation <20% who subsequently received preoperative intravenous iron infusion were compared with those who did not. Primary outcome was receipt of postoperative PRBC transfusion. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess predictors of transfusion. Negative binomial regression was used to model transfusion volume among transfused patients. RESULTS: Among 324 patients, 32 (9.9%) received preoperative intravenous iron and 59 (18.2%) required postoperative PRBC transfusion. Preoperative iron infusion was not independently associated with postoperative transfusion risk (aOR 1.26, 95% CI: 0.51-3.08, P = .62) or with number of PRBC units transfused (aIRR 1.00, 95% CI: 0.41-2.38, P = .997). Higher preoperative hemoglobin was associated with reduced transfusion risk (aOR 0.96 per g/L increase, 95% CI: 0.94-0.98, P < .001), while advanced tumor stage was associated with increased transfusion risk (aOR 2.55, 95% CI: 1.13-5.77, P = .024). These findings were unchanged in sensitivity analysis restricted to patients receiving iron ≥7 days preoperatively. CONCLUSION: Short-term iron repletion alone may be insufficient to mitigate transfusion requirements, highlighting the importance of earlier and/or more comprehensive anemia optimization strategies in this high-risk population.

Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70503
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42949233



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Oropharyngeal tumors with a propensity for submucosal spread can be difficult to detect and delineate during endoscopy. To facilitate their detection, we developed an Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithm to segment tumors and other anatomically significant structures within the oropharynx. STUDY DESIGN: Model development and validation study. SETTING: Tertiary academic medical center. METHODS: We collected videos from 106 patients undergoing pharyngolaryngoscopy, extracted 942 images, and annotated each pixel as one of 12 classes, such as tumor, uvula, and healthy mucosa. We trained an AI algorithm and evaluated its performance in multiclass and tumor-based segmentation. RESULTS: The AI algorithm achieved a recall statistic of 0.93 and a Dice score of 0.79 for tumor detection. High Dice scores were observed for pharyngeal mucosa (0.90), epiglottis (0.88), and vocal cords (0.82). CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that AI can semantically segment all the structures visualized during endoscopy, paving the way for computer-assisted systems for tumor identification and computer-assisted navigation during endoscopy or intubation.

item.title: Study on the Efficacy of Vidian Neurectomy in Combined Ocular-Nasal Therapy for Allergic Rhinoconjunctivitis.
item.dc:creator: Hu C, Liu G, Li C, Guo R, Wu K, Ding Y
item.description:
Authors: Hu C, Liu G, Li C, Guo R, Wu K, Ding Y
Journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1002/ohn.70483
Published: 2026-Oct-28
PMID: 42949223



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of vidian neurectomy (VN) in improving nasal and ocular symptoms in patients with drug-refractory allergic rhinoconjunctivitis (ARC). STUDY DESIGN: A prospective randomized controlled study. SETTING: Yiyang Central Hospital. METHODS: A total of 220 patients with drug-refractory ARC were allocated to the VN (n = 110) and fluticasone propionate (FP) (n = 110) groups. Clinical data, serum, and tear samples were collected at baseline and at 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, and 3 months after treatment. Serum immunoglobulin E (IgE), IgG, and IgA levels, tear meniscus height (TMH), tear break-up time (TBUT), tear secretion (via Schirmer's test [SIT]), and eosinophil cationic protein (ECP) and histamine (HA) were assessed. A 1-year follow-up was conducted to evaluate complications and recurrence, and the Kaplan-Meier curves were plotted to show the recurrence rates. RESULTS: Following treatment, patients in the VN group showed reduced serum IgE, IgG, IgA, ECP, and HA levels, and Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Sino-Nasal Outcome Test-20, Total Nasal Symptom Score, corneal fluorescein staining, and Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire scores, and increased TMH, TBUT, and SIT. Both groups demonstrated symptom relief (reduced VAS scores); however, the VN group achieved greater and more sustained improvement, particularly at 3 months, whereas the FP group plateaued after 1 month. Although complications were more frequent in the VN group, the 1-year recurrence rate was lower. CONCLUSION: VN significantly improves nasal and ocular symptoms, reduces immunologic and inflammatory markers, and lowers short-term recurrence in drug-refractory ARC, indicating favorable clinical potential.

item.title: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Energy Devices for Thyroidectomy: An Outcome-Specific Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.dc:creator: Kim DH, Jang DW, Hwang SH
item.description:
Authors: Kim DH, Jang DW, Hwang SH
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70524
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42947529



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: We performed an outcome-specific network meta-analysis comparing contemporary energy devices in thyroidectomy. METHODS: Randomized controlled trials comparing conventional hemostasis with Harmonic, LigaSure, Thunderbeat, or other advanced energy devices during thyroidectomy were included. Frequentist random-effects network meta-analyses were performed per outcome, with treatments ranked by P-scores and consistency assessed via design-by-treatment interaction and node-splitting analyses. RESULTS: Compared to conventional hemostasis, Harmonic significantly reduced operative time (SMD, -1.88), blood loss (SMD, -2.29), drainage volume (SMD, -1.77), hospital stay (SMD, -0.74), transient hypocalcemia (OR, 0.61), transient recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy (OR, 0.63), and postoperative bleeding (OR, 0.56). LigaSure improved operative efficiency but showed less consistent recovery and safety benefits. Harmonic ranked highest across most outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Harmonic showed the most favorable relative effects across the evaluated outcomes. However, these findings do not establish overall device superiority; selection should consider absolute benefits and device-specific characteristics.

item.title: Targeting Engrailed-1 Fibroblasts in Idiopathic Subglottic Stenosis.
item.dc:creator: Saeedi N, Collins SL, Lopez-Fay DC, Li YCC, Abd-Elazem I, Hillel AT, Motz KM
item.description:
Authors: Saeedi N, Collins SL, Lopez-Fay DC, Li YCC, Abd-Elazem I, Hillel AT, Motz KM
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71012
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42947382



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Idiopathic subglottic stenosis (iSGS) is characterized by pathologic deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) secondary to dysregulated fibroblasts. Engrailed-1 expressing fibroblasts have been shown to promote ECM deposition in fibrosis. Verteporfin has been shown to reduce EN1 expression in fibroblasts through YAP/TAZ signaling. However, EN1 expression, YAP/TAZ signaling, and verteporfin treatment have not been investigated in iSGS pathogenesis. METHODS: Biopsies of diseased subglottis and distal healthy trachea of iSGS patients (n = 6) were assessed. qRT-PCR, analysis of iSGS single-cell RNA sequencing data, flow cytometry and immunochemistry were used to compare the expression of EN1. Fibroblasts from diseased iSGS tissue were treated with verteporfin (5 μM) or control and gene and protein expression analysis was performed for EN1, YAP/TAZ pathway and fibrotic genes. RESULTS: The iSGS subglottis demonstrated increased expression of EN1 (fold change = 58.86, SD = 65.12, p: 0.031) compared to controls. Immunohistochemistry analysis of the diseased iSGS subglottis showed that EN1 was densely expressed. Verteporfin treatment of iSGS fibroblasts in vitro led to an 81.75% (SD = 9.28, p: 0.031) reduction in COL1A1 and 22.77% (SD = 17.11, p: 0.031) reduction in COL3A1 gene expression. This was associated with a 26.32% (SD = 28.25, p: 0.031) reduction in EN1 expression and reductions in the YAP/TAZ associated genes AMOTL2, CCN1, CCN2, YAP1, and WWTR1. CONCLUSION: EN1 and the associated YAP/TAZ signaling pathway are increased in iSGS. Verteporfin treatment inhibited YAP/TAZ expression and attenuated EN1 and COL1A1 expression in vitro. Targeting EN1 expressing fibroblasts through inhibition of YAP/TAZ signaling represents a potential therapeutic target to reduce fibrosis in iSGS. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

item.title: Preoperative Inflammatory Ratios Poorly Discriminate Malignant From Benign Parotid Tumours.
item.dc:creator: Kim JM, Jeon SY, Lee YC, Kim SI, Eun YG
item.description:
Authors: Kim JM, Jeon SY, Lee YC, Kim SI, Eun YG
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70536
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42946967



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether preoperative blood inflammatory ratios discriminate malignant from benign parotid tumours. METHODS: This retrospective single-centre study included 204 patients undergoing parotidectomy (45 malignant, 159 benign); inflammatory-index analyses included 45 malignant and 157 benign cases. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios were the two primary indices. Group differences were tested non-parametrically with multiplicity control, discrimination by receiver operating characteristic analysis and association by multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Median neutrophil-to-lymphocyte and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios were higher in malignant tumours (2.00 vs. 1.81 and 0.203 vs. 0.166), but effect sizes were small. Areas under the curve were 0.608 (95% confidence interval 0.518-0.701) and 0.631 (0.520-0.735), respectively. At the sample-derived neutrophil-to-lymphocyte threshold, sensitivity was 86.7% and specificity 35.7%. Additional inflammatory indices, histological subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses did not materially improve discrimination. CONCLUSIONS: Although the two primary ratios were higher in malignant tumours, their distributions overlapped substantially and discrimination was poor. These findings do not support their use as stand-alone markers for preoperative malignancy risk stratification.

item.title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity.
item.dc:creator: Smith GI, Petersen MC, Hartig SM, Klein S
item.description:
Authors: Smith GI, Petersen MC, Hartig SM, Klein S
Journal: Nature medicine | DOI: 10.1038/s41591-026-04718-7
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42946879



Abstract:
Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. A better understanding of the differences between metabolically divergent groups and the physiological responses to weight loss can help identify the factors responsible for the link between excess adiposity and metabolic dysfunction and disease.

item.title: Multidimensional Analysis of Immune Rejection in a Murine HLA-Mismatched Laryngeal Transplant Model.
item.dc:creator: Song Y, Li X, Wu T, Yu R, Gu D, Wang H, Liu J, Zhao Y, Ren J, Chen F
item.description:
Authors: Song Y, Li X, Wu T, Yu R, Gu D, Wang H, Liu J, Zhao Y, Ren J, Chen F
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.70987
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42946397



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To establish a murine heterotopic laryngeal transplantation (LT) model with a single HLA-A2 mismatch and to develop a multidimensional framework for dynamic evaluation of immune rejection and graft injury. METHODS: Laryngeal grafts from HLA-A2 transgenic mice were transplanted into C57BL/6 recipients to generate an HLA-mismatched LT model, with syngeneic C57BL/6 → C57BL/6 transplants as controls. A multidimensional evaluation system was established, integrating physiological monitoring (survival, body weight, graft appearance, neck circumference, computed tomography, and ultrasonography), immunological profiling (histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and flow cytometry), and inflammatory assessments (cytokines and biochemical parameters) from Day 0 to 12 weeks posttransplantation. RESULTS: Compared with syngeneic transplantation, the HLA-mismatched group showed aggravated immune rejection and graft injury. Progressive graft volume reduction was an early discriminator, detectable at 1 week posttransplantation and correlating with graft surface darkening and ulceration. Immunophenotyping revealed early CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell infiltration beginning at 1 week, whereas regulatory T cells increased at 3 days before markedly declining. Cytokine profiling showed elevations of MIP-1β, G-CSF, and IL-10 from 4 weeks onward, consistent with immune activation and graft injury. CONCLUSION: A murine heterotopic LT model with an HLA-A2 mismatch was established, demonstrating that a single HLA Class I disparity was sufficient to drive progressive immune rejection and graft injury in LT. A panel of biomarkers associated with adverse graft outcomes was observed, providing indicators for monitoring HLA-driven immune injury. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: N/A.

item.title: Duration of e-cigarette use and persistent symptoms in adolescents and young adults in the United States, 2020-2025.
item.dc:creator: Kreslake JM, Azadi M, McKay T, Schillo B
item.description:
Authors: Kreslake JM, Azadi M, McKay T, Schillo B
Journal: Preventive medicine | DOI: 10.1016/j.ypmed.2026.108686
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42946022



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess whether e-cigarette use is associated with subsequent health symptoms over time among young people in the United States. METHODS: Logistic regression analyses of online survey data from seven waves (2020-2025, N = 5917) of a probability-based longitudinal cohort (aged 15-24 years at enrollment) tested the association between e-cigarette use duration and subsequent persistent symptoms, controlling for other tobacco use, baseline self-rated health, and demographic characteristics. E-cigarette use was defined as: none (no use at any wave); experimental (use at 1 wave); sustained (use at ≥2 waves). Symptoms were defined as persistent if reported in past-month at ≥2 waves. RESULTS: Compared with no use, sustained e-cigarette use was associated with greater odds of persistent respiratory, somatic, and oral health symptoms at later waves. Significant associations included coughing/wheezing, chest pain/tightness, shortness of breath, difficulty sleeping, rapid heartbeat, high blood pressure, nausea/vomiting, weight changes, dry mouth/throat, and change/loss of taste (ORs: 1.43-2.84). Experimental use was associated with fewer persistent symptoms, including chest congestion, weight changes, dry mouth/throat, and change/loss of taste (ORs: 1.80-3.46). CONCLUSIONS: Findings support monitoring persistent symptoms associated with e-cigarette use, independent of other tobacco use, as potential indicators of longer-term health risks.

item.title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.
item.dc:creator: George S, Vaishampayan U, Hutson A, Groman A, Pili R, Green K, Herbst L, Kallicharan-Smith R, DiRaddo AM, Farrell E, et al.
item.description:
Authors: George S, Vaishampayan U, Hutson A, Groman A, Pili R, Green K, Herbst L, Kallicharan-Smith R, DiRaddo AM, Farrell E, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00394-3
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42945979



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls. METHODS: In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants. FINDINGS: Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred. INTERPRETATION: The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings. FUNDING: The Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (RPCCC), US National Cancer Institute (NCI), Novartis.

item.title: Chemoradiotherapy versus radiotherapy as adjuvant treatment for head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma: a meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Young TC, Yap WK, Chang KP, Lee YC, Lin CH, Cheng-En Hsieh R, Kang CJ, Fang KH, Tsai YT, Chen PY, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Young TC, Yap WK, Chang KP, Lee YC, Lin CH, Cheng-En Hsieh R, Kang CJ, Fang KH, Tsai YT, Chen PY, et al.
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108193
Published: 2026-Oct-27
PMID: 42945915



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The benefit of adding chemotherapy to postoperative radiotherapy for head and neck adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) remains uncertain. We compared adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) with radiotherapy (RT) alone. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception through May 6, 2026, with manual reference-list checking. Comparative studies reporting time-to-event outcomes for CRT versus RT were eligible. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and the Hartung-Knapp adjustment. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261485857). RESULTS: Eight studies contributed 836 outcome-specific observations. CRT was not associated with improved overall survival (six studies; 648 patients; HR, 0.99; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.70-1.41; I2 = 0%), disease-free/progression-free survival (five studies; 534 patients; HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.81-1.34; I2 = 0%), or distant metastasis-free survival (six studies; 574 patients; HR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.55-1.63; I2 = 44.5%). Neither locoregional control (two studies; 354 patients; HR, 0.09; 95% CI, 0.00-59.00) nor locoregional failure-free survival (three studies; 262 patients; HR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.32-2.60) improved significantly; both estimates were imprecise. Results were consistent in adjusted-versus-unadjusted subgroup and leave-one-out analyses. CONCLUSION: Available nonrandomized evidence does not demonstrate that adjuvant CRT improves survival compared with RT alone in head and neck ACC. Evidence for locoregional outcomes remains sparse and imprecise. These findings do not support routine chemotherapy but favor individualized treatment decisions.

item.title: Competence narrowing in AI-assisted oral English instruction: A quasi-experimental study of the spiral synergy framework.
item.dc:creator: Zhang J
item.description:
Authors: Zhang J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0357515
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945343



Abstract:
The rapid integration of generative AI tools into spoken English instruction has produced measurable fluency and accuracy gains, but whether these are evenly distributed across the dimensions of communicative competence remains underexplored. This quasi-experimental study compares the Spiral Synergy Framework (SSF), a three-layer pedagogical sequence (AI Consolidation, Bridging Tasks, Interpersonal Activation), against conventional AI-integrated instruction in two intact Business English classes at a Chinese higher vocational college (experimental n = 36, control n = 34), using oral recordings at three time points scored on five competence dimensions, 15 weeks of classroom observation, and an intra-rater reliability check. The two classes differed significantly at baseline on the oral composite score and three of five dimensions (control higher), though not on CET-4 proficiency or questionnaire items. Because treatment is confounded with class membership and both classes received AI-assisted practice, findings are reported as associations rather than demonstrated causal effects. Linear mixed-effects models testing Group × Time interactions across five outcomes (four dimensions and the composite), corrected for multiple comparisons, identified one outcome - real-time responsiveness - on which the classes diverged: the experimental class maintained responsiveness across the semester while the control class declined despite its baseline advantage (Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p = .029), a result that held under a cluster-robust sensitivity check. No corrected between-group difference was found for improvisation, coherence, naturalness, or the composite score; improvisation declined descriptively in both classes over the semester. Classroom observation data (experimental class only) document a recurring, non-monotonic cycle of AI-dependency reduction and rebound across 15 weeks. Intra-rater test-retest reliability of the oral-competence ratings was moderate to good (ICC = .67-.91), though this reflects a single rater familiar with participants rather than independent inter-rater agreement. Implications for multidimensional assessment, task sequencing, and cautious interpretation of AI-integrated curriculum research are discussed.

item.title: Safety assessment of microbial Polysaccharide Sanxan.
item.dc:creator: Zhang Y, Wu H, Pi J, Quan G, Chuo Q, Li X, Huang H
item.description:
Authors: Zhang Y, Wu H, Pi J, Quan G, Chuo Q, Li X, Huang H
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361184
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945291



Abstract:
This study evaluated the oral safety of Sanxan to provide a basis for its application in food. The toxicological characteristics of Sanxan were assessed through an acute oral toxicity test, three genetic toxicity tests, a teratogenicity test in pregnant rats, and a 90-day oral toxicity test. The results showed that no obvious toxic symptoms or mortality were observed in the acute toxicity test, and the maximum tolerated dose was greater than 15 g/kg, indicating that Sanxan had no acute oral toxicity in the test animals. The results of three genetic toxicity tests-the Ames test, the micronucleus test, and the sperm abnormality test-were all negative, and the teratogenicity test in pregnant rats showed no maternal toxicity, embryotoxicity, or teratogenicity, indicating that Sanxan had no mutagenic or teratogenic effects under the tested conditions. The 90-day oral toxicity test showed that Sanxan at doses of 1.3, 2.6, and 5.2 g/kg body weight had no obvious adverse effects on body weight gain, total food intake, total food utilization, hematology, serum biochemistry, organ-to-body weight ratios, or pathological examination in the test animals, and the maximum no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) was 5.2 g/kg body weight. In summary, under the conditions of this study, Sanxan did not exhibit acute toxicity, genetic toxicity, teratogenicity, or subchronic toxicity, indicating that it has good safety under the tested conditions.

item.title: Airway management and anaesthetic interventions for children with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Sumi SA, Arin KM, Shams SM, Rafique T, Orchi K, Chowdhury A, Rahman MM, Haque MA
item.description:
Authors: Sumi SA, Arin KM, Shams SM, Rafique T, Orchi K, Chowdhury A, Rahman MM, Haque MA
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361327
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945279



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with cleft lip and/or palate may present unique challenges during perioperative airway management because of altered upper-airway and craniofacial anatomy. These children frequently undergo surgical procedures requiring general anaesthesia and airway instrumentation. Several airway-management and anaesthetic techniques have been evaluated to facilitate tracheal intubation and reduce perioperative airway complications, but the comparative evidence from randomised controlled trials has not been systematically evaluated. METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis will include randomised controlled trials involving children < 18 years with cleft lip and/or palate undergoing general anaesthesia. Eligible studies will compare alternative techniques or devices for airway management or other anaesthetic strategies between two groups of cleft lip/palate patients. The primary outcome will be difficulty in tracheal intubation. Where definitions vary substantially, outcomes will be analysed separately or synthesised narratively. Secondary outcomes will include difficult mask ventilation, oxygen desaturation, airway obstruction, difficult laryngoscopy, first-attempt intubation success, number of intubation attempts, time to successful intubation or airway establishment, failed intubation and other perioperative airway or respiratory adverse events. Two reviewers will independently select RCTs, extract data and assess risk of bias. Risk of bias will be evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Random-effects meta-analysis will be performed where clinically appropriate. Risk ratios will be used for dichotomous outcomes and mean differences or standardized mean differences for continuous outcomes. Certainty of evidence for important outcomes will be assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. REGISTRATION AND REVIEW STATUS: The review was prospectively registered in PROSPERO on 10 March 2026 (CRD420261326076). Full-text screening and data extraction are ongoing and not yet complete. Protocol amendments are documented transparently in PROSPERO.

item.title: Photobiomodulation versus stabilization splint, both combined with self-management, for acute temporomandibular myalgia: 48-week outcomes of a partially randomized controlled study.
item.dc:creator: Hoa NN, Do T, Hoang VH, Thanh Dong T, Quyen TTM, Binh TT
item.description:
Authors: Hoa NN, Do T, Hoang VH, Thanh Dong T, Quyen TTM, Binh TT
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360472
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945268



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Photobiomodulation (LLLT) is used for myogenous temporomandibular disorders (TMD), but longer-term comparative evidence versus stabilization splints alongside structured self-management remains limited. This study aims to compare pain reduction and maximum painless mouth opening after photobiomodulation+self-management (PBM + SM) versus stabilization splint+self-management (OS + SM), with an additional self-management-only comparator (SM), over 48 weeks. METHODS: This partially randomized controlled study enrolled 66 patients with DC/TMD-diagnosed acute masticatory muscle pain. Forty-four participants consenting to intervention were randomized 1:1 to PBM + SM (660-nm diode laser, twice weekly, 10 sessions) or OS + SM (maxillary stabilization splint worn at night, 8 h/day for 2 months). Both intervention groups received the same SM programme (education, habit modification, and jaw exercises for 2 months). A non-randomized convenience group received SM alone (n = 22). Assessments were performed at baseline and weeks 2, 4, 12, 24, and 48. Primary outcomes were VAS pain (0-10) and maximum painless mouth opening (MPMO, mm). Secondary outcomes included masticatory muscle tenderness and Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC). Longitudinal analyses used linear mixed-effects models. RESULTS: All groups improved over time, with earlier improvement in both intervention arms. In the randomized comparison, PBM + SM and OS + SM showed comparable week-48 outcomes for VAS pain and MPMO. No significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points was observed at week 48 after Holm adjustment. Comparisons involving the SM-only group were exploratory. CONCLUSIONS: Over 48 weeks, PBM + SM and OS + SM produced comparable improvements in pain and maximum painless mouth opening, with no significant between-group difference in masticatory muscle tender points at week 48. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06419738.

item.title: Buccal and sublingual lyophilised naloxone for opioid overdose reversal: A Phase 1 open-label, random-sequence crossover pharmacokinetic study protocol in healthy volunteers (NalBuc).
item.dc:creator: Gonzalez Utrilla M, Baker A, Chesney E, Lee K, Emsley R, Strang J
item.description:
Authors: Gonzalez Utrilla M, Baker A, Chesney E, Lee K, Emsley R, Strang J
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0347370
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42945264



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Opioid overdose remains a major global public health emergency, with naloxone being an essential response. Benefit from existing naloxone formulations is limited by barriers to acceptability, fixed dosing, and poor real-world carriage. This study describes the protocol for a Phase 1 exploratory investigation of a novel ultra-portable lyophilised naloxone wafer designed to facilitate constant carriage and enable rapid mucosal absorption. METHODS: This open-label, randomised, random-sequence, five-way crossover pharmacokinetic (PK) exploratory study will recruit 12-15 healthy adults at a UK clinical research facility. Participants will receive five treatments, each separated by ≥36 hours: buccal naloxone wafer 2 mg, buccal wafer 4 mg, sublingual wafer 2 mg, intramuscular naloxone 0.4 mg, and intranasal naloxone 1.8 mg (Nyxoid®). Blood samples will be collected up to 240 minutes post-dose for PK analysis via validated LC-MS/MS methods. The primary endpoint is time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax). Secondary endpoints include Maximum Plasma Concentration (Cmax), Time to 50% of maximum concentration (T50%), Area Under the Curve from time zero to 15 minutes (AUC0-15), Area Under the Curve from time zero to infinity (AUCinf), and safety/tolerability. Dose-proportionality and buccal-sublingual comparisons will be explored. Trial Registration:REC: 25/LO/0701; MHRA CTA (IRAS): 1011060. ISRCTN67173532. RESULTS & SIGNIFICANCE: This study will characterise the absorption profile, early exposure, and relative bioavailability of a novel naloxone wafer formulated for rapid buccal and sublingual administration. Findings will inform whether this technology could provide a practical, effective alternative to current injectable and intranasal products, with potential to substantially improve naloxone carriage and timely overdose response, and will guide the design of a subsequent, larger confirmatory study.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) rs671 (G>A) variant, common in East Asians, impairs aldehyde detoxification. Pathogenic germline variants (PGVs) in homologous recombination repair (HRR) and mismatch repair (MMR) genes confer inherited susceptibility; however, their joint effects with rs671 remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We conducted a case-control study of 4,418 cases of head and neck, esophageal, gastric, or colorectal cancer and 11,811 controls. Targeted sequencing identified HRR and MMR PGVs. RESULTS: HRR PGV carriers with the rs671 GA/AA genotype showed increased risk across all cancer sites compared with rs671 GG non-carriers. Joint effects were observed among drinkers for head and neck, esophageal, and gastric cancers, and among non-drinkers for gastric and colorectal cancers. item.title: Helicobacter pylori Infection Is Associated With the Occurrence and Progression of Vocal Fold Leukoplakia via NRF2/KEAP1 Pathway Activation.

Journal: International journal of cancer | DOI: 10.1002/ijc.70668
Published: 2026-Oct-27

Abstract:
Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection has been implicated in vocal fold leukoplakia (VFL), a precancerous laryngeal lesion. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the relationship between H. pylori and VFL, focusing on the NRF2/KEAP1 oxidative stress pathway. Clinicopathological analysis was performed on samples from 64 patients with VFL and 30 patients with vocal cord polyps (controls). The results showed a significantly higher prevalence of H. pylori in the VFL group (48.4%) than in the controls (16.7%, p = 0.003). Among H. pylori-positive VFL cases, VacA-positive strains predominated, accounting for 71.0%. Multivariate logistic regression identified H. pylori as an independent risk factor for VFL (OR = 6.198, 95% CI: 1.580-24.321). VFL tissues exhibited upregulated expression of NRF2, KEAP1, and HO-1 (p < 0.001), demonstrating both virulence-dependent (HO-1 induction) and virulence-independent (NRF2 upregulation) pathway activation patterns. In vitro experiments revealed that H. pylori exposure induced NRF2 nuclear translocation and triggered an oxidative stress response. Furthermore, VFL-derived cells displayed more pronounced stress-induced morphological alterations following H. pylori exposure. These findings suggest that H. pylori may promote VFL progression via NRF2/KEAP1 pathway activation, highlighting the potential clinical value of H. pylori screening in VFL management.

item.title: The Evolution and Clinical Utility of Oral Epithelial Dysplasia Grading Systems: A Narrative Review.
item.dc:creator: Ramanathan A, Tilakaratne WM

Authors: Ramanathan A, Tilakaratne WM
Journal: Oral diseases | DOI: 10.1111/odi.70553
Published: 2026-Oct-27

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Histological grading of oral epithelial dysplasia (OED) is the gold standard for predicting malignant transformation in potentially malignant disorders. However, traditional grading systems suffer from subjectivity and poor diagnostic reproducibility, complicating patient management. This narrative review evaluates the clinical utility of current and emerging OED grading systems. METHODS: We reviewed recent literature (2019-2026) comparing the traditional World Health Organization (WHO) classifications against binary grading, histopathological feature-specific models (two-point and six-point systems), diagnostic biomarkers, and clinical risk factors. RESULTS: The WHO system frequently demonstrates poor-to-fair interobserver agreement. Conversely, binary and six-point grading systems provide superior reproducibility. While these models effectively stratify malignant transformation risk, their clinical utility is limited by tissue sampling errors, such as "skip areas." Furthermore, immunohistochemical biomarkers (Keratin 13 and 17) show promise as diagnostic adjuncts to assist in identifying high-risk variants like differentiated dysplasia. CONCLUSION: While the WHO system remains the gold standard, its subjectivity complicates clinical decisions. Adopting objective binary and feature-specific models offers superior clinical utility for risk stratification. Clear numerical cutoffs alongside expanded morphological features and biomarkers may influence the accuracy of predicting malignant transformation, inform clinical decision-making regarding surgical versus conservative surveillance, and optimize patient management when integrated with clinicopathological findings.

item.title: Recurrence Risk in Lateralized Floor of Mouth Carcinoma: Depth of Invasion Versus Midline Distance.

item.description:

Published: 2026-Oct-26

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contralateral nodal recurrence in lateralized floor-of-mouth squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) remains difficult to predict, and objective preoperative parameters to guide contralateral neck management in tumors without midline crossing are lacking. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 97 patients with lateral floor-of-mouth OSCC treated by surgical resection and neck dissection. Depth of invasion (DOI) was evaluated using endpoint-specific univariable Cox regression. Contralateral nodal disease was analyzed in patients without midline crossing (n = 68) using a composite endpoint of occult contralateral nodal metastasis and/or subsequent contralateral nodal recurrence. Tumor-to-midline distance was assessed on standardized multiplanar preoperative CT or MRI. RESULTS: DOI was associated with local recurrence (HR 1.322 per mm, 95% CI 1.131-1.545, p < 0.001) and ipsilateral regional recurrence (HR 1.199, 95% CI 1.052-1.367, p = 0.007), but not with contralateral recurrence (HR 1.030, 95% CI 0.834-1.272, p = 0.782). Among 68 patients without midline crossing, no occult contralateral metastases were identified in 19 clinically contralateral node-negative patients undergoing elective contralateral neck dissection. Four patients (5.9%) developed subsequent contralateral nodal recurrence. Midline distance was smaller in patients with an event (median 3.15 vs. 6.40 mm; p = 0.022; AUC 0.845). All four events occurred at < 5 mm (4/21 [19.0%] vs. 0/42 [0%]; Fisher p = 0.010). In time-to-event analysis, greater midline distance was associated with a lower hazard of contralateral recurrence (HR 0.622 per mm, 95% CI 0.395-0.981, p = 0.041). CONCLUSION: DOI showed an outcome-specific association with local and ipsilateral, but not contralateral, recurrence. In tumors without midline crossing, quantitative proximity to the midline was associated with subsequent contralateral nodal failure. The observed 5-mm threshold is exploratory and requires external validation before it can inform clinical decision-making.

item.title: Targeting the lactate receptor GPR81 suppresses tumor progression by disrupting glycolytic metabolism in oral squamous cell carcinoma.
item.dc:creator: Okuda A, Funayama N, Hata K, Sugiyama M, Kobayashi-Ichiyama S, Wakamori K, Li LJ, Hirose K, Usami Y, Omi-Sugihara M, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Okuda A, Funayama N, Hata K, Sugiyama M, Kobayashi-Ichiyama S, Wakamori K, Li LJ, Hirose K, Usami Y, Omi-Sugihara M, et al.
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108188
Published: 2026-Oct-26
PMID: 42933364



Abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cancer cells reprogram glucose metabolism toward aerobic glycolysis, a phenomenon known as the Warburg effect. This metabolic shift results in substantial lactate accumulation within the tumor microenvironment. Although lactate has been implicated in tumor aggressiveness, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Recent studies have identified lactate as an active signaling molecule that exerts its effects through G-protein-coupled receptor 81 (GPR81). The present study aimed to elucidate the clinical and functional significance of GPR81 in the progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: GPR81 expression was evaluated using human OSCC tissue specimens (n = 84). In vitro functional assays and xenograft studies were performed using GPR81-knockdown HSC-3 and SAS cell lines. The role of GPR81 in oral carcinogenesis was further examined using an immunocompetent 4-nitroquinoline 1-oxide (4-NQO)-induced carcinogenesis model in Gpr81 knockout mice. RESULTS: GPR81 expression was significantly higher in OSCC specimens than in normal oral mucosa. GPR81 knockdown suppressed cell proliferation and tumor formation in OSCC models. In the 4-NQO-induced carcinogenesis model, the area of squamous cell carcinoma within the tongue was significantly reduced in Gpr81 knockout mice compared with wild-type controls. Mechanistically, GPR81 knockdown reduced ATP production and was associated with decreased expression of glycolytic genes including PFKL, PKM2 and LDHA. CONCLUSION: Through a multi-model approach, we identify GPR81 as an important regulator of oral carcinogenesis via glycolytic reprogramming. These findings suggest that targeting the lactate-GPR81 signaling axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for aggressive OSCC.

item.title: Epidemiological characterization of avian influenza virus circulation in pigeons and quail across different production systems in Chattogram, Bangladesh.
item.dc:creator: Habib MI, Sayeed MA, Islam M, Sarker MFR, Shakil SS, Hassan MM, Forwood JK, Ahad A, Islam A
item.description:
Authors: Habib MI, Sayeed MA, Islam M, Sarker MFR, Shakil SS, Hassan MM, Forwood JK, Ahad A, Islam A
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361561
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
Pigeons and quail contribute to poultry production, nutrition, and livelihoods in Bangladesh; however, their role in avian influenza virus (AIV) circulation remains poorly understood. These poultry species are widely reared and traded alongside chickens and ducks in household farms, commercial systems, and live bird markets, where inadequate biosecurity may create an overlooked ecological niche for AIV circulation, reassortment, and potential zoonotic spillover. Between November 2021 and April 2022, we conducted a cross-sectional study in Chattogram, Bangladesh, to estimate the prevalence and subtype-specific distribution of AIV and to identify factors associated with AIV positivity in pigeons and quail. A total of 300 birds (108 pigeons and 192 quail) were sampled from households, commercial farms, and live bird markets. Oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs were collected from each bird and tested for the AIV matrix gene using real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by subtype-specific detection of H5, H7, and H9. Data collected from bird owners and traders included bird demographic characteristics, bird source, and health status using a structured questionnaire. The overall prevalence of AIV was 14.3% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 10.6-18.8). Quail had a higher prevalence (18.2%, 95% CI: 13.0-24.4) than pigeons (7.4%, 95% CI: 3.3-14.1). Among detected subtypes, H9 was most prevalent (11.3%, 95% CI: 7.9-15.4), followed by hemagglutinin (HA)-untyped (2.7%, 95% CI: 1.2-5.1) and H5 (0.3%, 95% CI: 0.001-1.8), while H7 was not detected. Quail had higher odds of AIV positivity than pigeons (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.1, 95% CI: 1.8-10.6); clinically sick birds (aOR = 2.9, 95% CI: 1.4-6.2) and birds sampled from household farms (aOR = 2.8, 95% CI: 1.2-6.5) also had higher odds of AIV positivity. These findings indicate that pigeons and quails, which are understudied poultry species, may contribute to the maintenance and transmission of AIV within mixed poultry production and marketing systems in Bangladesh. Integrating these species into routine AIV surveillance is therefore necessary to strengthen early detection, inform control strategies, and reduce the risk of zoonotic spillover.

item.title: Oral versus vaginal Lactobacillus supplementation for endometrial dysbiosis: A paired pre and post-endometrial microbiome study.
item.dc:creator: Hiratsuka D, Iki A, Kinoshita M, Doi Y, Kato O, Oshima K, Hiraoka T, Matsuo M, Ichinose M, Makabe T, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Hiratsuka D, Iki A, Kinoshita M, Doi Y, Kato O, Oshima K, Hiraoka T, Matsuo M, Ichinose M, Makabe T, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0360619
Published: 2026-01-01
