Abstract:
Infertility is a global health challenge, and impaired endometrial receptivity remains an important contributor to treatment failure. Endometrial dysbiosis, characterized by a low proportion of Lactobacillus in the endometrial microbiota, has been proposed as a potentially modifiable factor that may affect endometrial receptivity and fertility, and treatment with Lactobacillus-containing probiotics is emerging as a promising therapeutic approach. However, the optimal route of Lactobacillus supplementation remains unclear. We compared oral versus vaginal supplementation using the same Lactobacillus-containing formulation as an adjunct to standardized doxycycline/metronidazole therapy and continued oral lactoferrin in patients with baseline endometrial Lactobacillus <10%, based on paired microbiome profiling of endometrial samples (aspirated intrauterine fluid and endometrial tissue). In this single-center retrospective cohort study, thirty-two patients underwent paired endometrial microbiome testing before and after 30 days of supplementation (oral, n = 18; vaginal, n = 14). In the vaginal group, the median endometrial Lactobacillus proportion increased from 0.05% [0.00-0.20] to 99.15% [70.45-100.00] (p = 0.001), whereas in the oral group it increased from 0.00% [0.00-0.18] to 0.30% [0.03-66.33] (p = 0.005). The median change was greater with vaginal versus oral supplementation (+98.90% [70.45-99.80] vs + 0.25% [0.03-66.33], p < 0.001). Post-treatment Lactobacillus ≥80%, used as an exploratory marker of marked microbiota improvement, was observed in 9/14 patients (64%) in the vaginal group and 3/18 (17%) in the oral group (p = 0.010). Exploratory reproductive outcomes were limited by the small sample size and did not define a reliable clinical threshold. These findings suggest that, within this combined treatment regimen, vaginal Lactobacillus supplementation may provide a greater route-associated additional improvement in endometrial microbiota profiles than oral administration.

item.title: The combination of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine in lidocaine ice popsicle compared with lidocaine ice popsicle alone in patients undergoing unsedated esophagogastroduodenoscopy: A prospective double-blind randomized controlled trial.
item.dc:creator: Intarasangkhanawin P, Orrapin S, Anuponganan W, Soonthornkes N, Mahawongkajit P
item.description:
Authors: Intarasangkhanawin P, Orrapin S, Anuponganan W, Soonthornkes N, Mahawongkajit P
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361495
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42932276



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal mucosal visualization is essential for high-quality esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), particularly for the detection of subtle upper gastrointestinal lesions. Oral simethicone and N-acetylcysteine (NAC) are commonly used to improve mucosal cleanliness, whereas lidocaine ice popsicles provide effective topical pharyngeal anesthesia for unsedated EGD. We evaluated whether incorporating simethicone and NAC into a lidocaine ice popsicle could improve mucosal visibility while maintaining patient comfort. METHODS: This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 374 adults undergoing unsedated diagnostic EGD between December 2024 and June 2025. Participants were randomized (1:1) to receive either a lidocaine ice popsicle containing simethicone (100 mg) and NAC (600 mg) or a conventional lidocaine ice popsicle. The primary outcome was mucosal visibility assessed using a modified Total Visibility Score (TVS). Secondary outcomes included procedure time, water volume required for mucosal cleansing, additional simethicone use, endoscopist satisfaction, ease of esophageal instrumentation, gag reflex, patient satisfaction, discomfort, pain, and adverse events. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 25.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). RESULTS: All 374 randomized participants (187 per group) completed the study and were analyzed according to their assigned groups. Baseline characteristics were descriptively similar between groups. The intervention group had a significantly lower TVS than the control group (6.19 ± 0.51 vs. 10.39 ± 2.22; mean difference, -4.20; 95% CI, -4.53 to -3.88; P < 0.001), indicating better mucosal visibility. Exploratory segment-specific analyses showed lower visibility scores in all six gastrointestinal segments. The intervention group also had higher endoscopist satisfaction, shorter procedure time (10.87 ± 1.44 vs. 12.75 ± 0.96 min; P < 0.001), lower water requirements for mucosal cleansing, and less frequent use of additional diluted simethicone during EGD (12.8% vs. 96.8%; P < 0.001). Exploratory analyses showed statistically significant differences in gag reflex and pain scores, although the absolute differences were small. Patient satisfaction, discomfort, and ease of esophageal instrumentation did not differ significantly between groups. No adverse events were observed during the defined observation period. CONCLUSIONS: The combined formulation of simethicone and N-acetylcysteine incorporated into a lidocaine ice popsicle improved mucosal visibility compared with a lidocaine ice popsicle alone during unsedated EGD and was associated with improved procedural efficiency. This integrated formulation may provide a practical approach to pre-endoscopic preparation by combining topical anesthesia with mucosal cleansing. Further multicenter studies are warranted to confirm its effectiveness, generalizability, and safety with longer follow-up. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20240606004.

item.title: Low- and intermediate-grade, low-stage primary parotid cancer: does a "partial" surgery impair disease control? a multicenter retrospective study.
item.dc:creator: Galli A, Tomasoni M, Salerno E, Di Santo D, Ferrari M, Missale F, Borsetto D, Mazzola F, Low TH, Gupta R, et al.
item.description:

Published: 2026-Oct-26

Abstract:
PURPOSE: Primary parotid malignancies are rare and heterogeneous. While comprehensive surgery with postoperative radiotherapy (PORT) is well established for high-grade and/or advanced-stage disease, the optimal management of lower grade, early-stage parotid carcinomas remains debatable due to their indolent behavior and low risk of nodal spread. METHODS: A multicenter retrospective analysis was conducted across ten tertiary referral centers. Patients with primary parotid carcinomas staged as pT1-T2 cN0/pNx and classified as low/intermediate-grade were included (2000-2020). Surgical procedures were categorized as partial (extracapsular dissection, partial superficial, superficial, selective deep lobe parotidectomy) or comprehensive. Time to recurrence (TTR), recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 129 patients met the inclusion criteria. Partial surgery was performed in 75.4% of cases, and PORT was administered in 37.8%. The 5-year TTR, RFS and OS was 96.6%, 91.7%, and 94.9%, respectively. Recurrence occurred in 3.9% of patients, with no regional failures and no disease-related deaths. PNI was linked to shorter TTR (HR 17.3, p = 0.002), whereas intermediate grade (HR 3.17, p = 0.035), older age (HR 1.03, p = 0.050), pT2 (HR 2.96, p = 0.045) and PNI (HR 4.68, p = 0.009) were associated with lower RFS. Only age was associated with reduced OS. The extent of surgery and PORT did not significantly influence TTR, RFS or OS. CONCLUSIONS: Low/intermediate-grade early-stage parotid carcinomas showed excellent oncologic outcomes in our cohort, in which we did not find an association between the extent of surgery performed and relapse or survival. item.title: Supraglottic airway vs. endotracheal tube for sinonasal surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Cuddeford A, Mubaarak Z, Yussuf B, Ali S, Mavadia A, Gao C, Devabalan Y, Dhanani R, Zaidi AK, Iftikhar H
item.description:

Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10650-w

PMID: 42931838



Abstract:
PURPOSE: This systematic review evaluates the relative safety and side-effect profiles of endotracheal tubes (ETs) and supraglottic airway devices (SGAs) for airway management in endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). METHODS: A search of MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library was conducted in April 2025. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed for outcomes reported by three or more studies with comparable methodology; remaining outcomes were synthesised narratively. Primary outcomes were aspiration events, airway contamination and adverse post-operative symptoms (cough, sore throat, hoarseness, nausea and vomiting); secondary outcomes were operative time and estimated blood loss. Nine studies (714 patients, 1995-2024) were eligible. RESULTS: Aspiration was rare (one asymptomatic ET case). Pooled analysis demonstrated a significant reduction in airway contamination with SGA use (RR 0.27, 95% CI 0.15-0.47, I²=0%). Device contamination was common in both (SGAs 0-86%, ETs 53-77%) but of limited clinical consequence. Pooled analysis also demonstrated a significant reduction in post-operative day 0 cough with SGA use (RR 0.39, 95% CI 0.23-0.68, I²=0%), whereas day 0 sore throat showed no significant difference (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.24-1.74, I²=68.7%). Trends toward reduced hoarse voice, blood loss and operative time favoured SGAs but were not significant. CONCLUSION: The historical concern that SGAs offer inferior airway protection during ESS is not supported by current comparative evidence. In appropriately selected, low-aspiration-risk patients, SGAs represent a safe alternative to ETs. Given the heterogeneous evidence base, findings should assist rather than replace clinical judgment, with device selection guided by individual patient and procedural factors.

item.title: Effects of aging and bolus characteristics on laryngeal movement during oropharyngeal swallowing.
item.dc:creator: Lee SH, Hsieh LC, Yan JY, Lee GS
item.description:
Authors: Lee SH, Hsieh LC, Yan JY, Lee GS
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10686-y
Published: 2026-Oct-26
PMID: 42931835



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Swallowing is a complex sensorimotor process that dynamically adapts to bolus characteristics and physiological variations. Age-related neuromuscular changes in older adults can alter swallowing function, potentially compromising swallowing safety and efficiency. This study investigated age-related differences in oropharyngeal swallowing by analyzing laryngeal displacement and swallowing sounds using a force-sensitive resistor (FSR) sensor and cervical auscultation. METHODS: Six swallowing tasks with varying bolus volumes and viscosities were assessed across 16 healthy young adults and 12 healthy older adults. A two-way mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of variance was conducted to examine differences in temporal and amplitude parameters of the acoustic and FSR signals. RESULTS: FSR signals analysis revealed that increasing bolus volumes shorten the duration of laryngeal activation in young adults, whereas it produced significantly prolonged laryngeal activation in older adults. Additionally, aging significantly increased the overall duration of laryngeal movement during swallowing, particularly during the relaxation phase. No significant gender effects were observed in any of the analyses. CONCLUSIONS: In older adults, slower laryngeal movement during the oropharyngeal phase of swallowing indicates reduced muscular capacity and diminished coordination between bolus transit and laryngeal kinematics. These age-related neuromuscular changes may compromise swallowing efficiency and airway protection, thereby increasing susceptibility to dysphagia-related complications. Future research should focus on developing automated detection algorithms and multimodal datasets that combine physiological measurements and swallowing imaging to objectively link sensor-derived features to physiological swallowing events.

item.title: Fat graft-reinforced repair of refractory cervical chyle leak after neck dissection.
item.dc:creator: Roh JL
item.description:
Authors: Roh JL
Journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery | DOI: 10.1007/s00405-026-10679-x
Published: 2026-Oct-26
PMID: 42931831



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Chyle leak is an uncommon but clinically significant complication after neck dissection, particularly in the left lower neck, where the thoracic duct is most vulnerable. High-output or persistent leakage may result in metabolic derangement, wound complications, and delayed recovery. Surgical intervention becomes necessary when conservative management is unsuccessful. This study describes a standardized surgical technique combining targeted lymphatic ligation with autologous abdominal fat graft reinforcement and reports its clinical outcomes. METHODS: Five patients who developed refractory or high-output chyle leak after neck dissection at a university hospital cancer center underwent surgical repair. Conservative measures, including dietary fat restriction, pressure dressing, closed suction drainage, and octreotide, were employed before surgery. Operative management consisted of precisely identifying the leaking lymphatic channel, ligation with 4 - 0 polypropylene sutures, and placement of a peri-umbilical fat graft to reinforce the repair. RESULTS: All patients showed immediate cessation of chyle leakage following surgery. None required reoperation, thoracic duct embolization, or thoracoscopic intervention. A regular oral diet was resumed within 3-5 days, and all patients were discharged without complications. Follow-up assessments confirmed durable resolution without recurrence or donor-site morbidity. CONCLUSION: Targeted lymphatic ligation combined with autologous fat grafting reinforcement was technically feasible and was associated with successful leak control in this small descriptive case series. Larger comparative studies are required to define the independent contribution of fat graft reinforcement.

item.title: Head and neck cancer in older adults: biological aging, treatment tolerance, and survivorship.
item.dc:creator: Bou Zerdan M, Assi J, Bouferraa Y, Abu Faraj J, Bilani N, Brammer B, Castro EA, Abi Zeid Daou C, Stokes WA, Rudra S, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Bou Zerdan M, Assi J, Bouferraa Y, Abu Faraj J, Bilani N, Brammer B, Castro EA, Abi Zeid Daou C, Stokes WA, Rudra S, et al.
Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute | DOI: 10.1093/jnci/djag332
Published: 2026-Oct-26
PMID: 42929787



Abstract:
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNC) is increasingly diagnosed in older adults, a population characterized by substantial heterogeneity in physiologic reserve, comorbidity burden, functional status, and social support. Chronological age alone is an inadequate predictor of treatment tolerance and outcomes, yet it continues to influence therapeutic decision-making despite growing evidence supporting individualized assessment. This review summarizes the current evidence on aging and HNC, emphasizing the impact of comorbidities, frailty, comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA), and biological aging on treatment selection, toxicity, and survival. We review validated geriatric assessment tools, including frailty measures and evaluation of cognitive, nutritional, and social domains, which consistently provide prognostic information beyond age and conventional performance status. Emerging data on immunologic aging and other biomarkers of biological aging suggest promising avenues for improving risk stratification, although these approaches remain investigational. We also discuss evidence from contemporary clinical trials, treatment adaptation and de-escalation strategies, implementation science, and the persistent underrepresentation of older adults in oncology research. Survivorship challenges, including late toxicities, functional decline, rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary long-term care, are reviewed alongside disparities in access to care that disproportionately affect older patients. Collectively, the available evidence supports a shift from age-based treatment decisions toward individualized care guided by physiologic reserve, geriatric assessment, and patient-centered goals. Future progress will depend on integrating geroscience, validated biomarkers of biological aging, geriatric-informed clinical trial design, and implementation strategies that improve equitable access to evidence-based care for the growing population of older adults with HNC.

Authors: Deng H, Wang J, Yuan T, Lai X, Kong W, Xiong X, Yang Q, Wu X, Zheng B, Shi Z
Journal: Head & neck | DOI: 10.1002/hed.70504

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporalis muscle flap (TMF) reconstruction is common for postradiation skull base osteoradionecrosis (ORN). However, the whole TMF may be too large, causing difficult tunnel passage, tearing, and choanal atresia, while an overly small TMF risks pedicle damage and incomplete coverage. Safely harvesting an appropriate TMF remains challenging. We evaluated the feasibility and long-term outcome of precise TMF splitting and explored necrosis risk factors. STUDY DESIGN: Prospective, single-arm clinical study. SETTING: Comparison of inter-group ultrasonographic parameters of the anterior/posterior deep temporal arteries (ADTA/PDTA), analyzed flap survival rate, risk factors for flap necrosis. METHODS: Sixty ORN patients who underwent TMF reconstruction were included. Preoperative ultrasonography mapped ADTA/PDTA to guide TMF splitting. Surgical outcomes and complications were recorded. Univariate analysis and multivariate Firth's penalized logistic regression were used to identify independent risk factors for flap necrosis. RESULTS: Overall flap survival rate was 95.00% (57/60). Univariate analysis identified prolonged operative time (p = 0.006), tumor recurrence (p = 0.049), and low preoperative prealbumin (p = 0.033) as risk factors. Multivariate analysis confirmed operative time as an independent risk factor (OR = 1.007, p = 0.035). The optimal operative time cutoff for predicting necrosis was 635 min (AUC = 0.824, p = 0.032), which is presented as an exploratory threshold requiring validation in future cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: Precise TMF harvesting is suitable for predominantly unilateral nasopharyngeal reconstruction, especially for necrosis invading the internal carotid artery, avoiding complications such as temporal depression, choanal atresia/stenosis from an oversized flap, and necrosis from difficult tunnel passage.

item.title: Osimertinib-Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy. METHODS: In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety. RESULTS: Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group. CONCLUSIONS: Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Divarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib. METHODS: In this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety. RESULTS: A total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. item.title: Technical optimization in adenotonsillar surgery: A practical narrative review of strategies to improve surgical exposure, safety, and visualization.
item.dc:creator: Lorente-Piera J, Cervera-Paz FJ
item.description:
Authors: Lorente-Piera J, Cervera-Paz FJ
Journal: American journal of otolaryngology | DOI: 10.1016/j.amjoto.2026.104968
Published: 2026-Oct-24
PMID: 42945818



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To critically synthesize and integrate intraoperative technical strategies designed to optimize visualization, surgical exposure, tissue protection, and/or hemostatic control during adenotonsillar surgery. METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library to identify studies published between January 1996 and May 2026. The search strategy combined MeSH terms and free-text keywords related to adenotonsillectomy, operative visualization, surgical exposure, hemostasis, tissue protection, microscopy, endoscopy, and suction-assisted techniques. Following title and abstract screening and full-text assessment, 38 studies were included in the final qualitative synthesis. RESULTS: The available evidence indicates that multiple complementary intraoperative strategies can improve operative precision and surgical safety during adenotonsillar surgery. Microscope- and endoscope-assisted techniques enhance anatomical visualization, facilitate targeted hemostasis, and improve the identification of residual lymphoid tissue and occult bleeding sites. Cheek expanders and modified retraction systems increase transverse surgical exposure and improve instrument maneuverability. Protective measures, including salivary cotton rolls and moist gauze, may reduce pressure- and thermal-related mucosal injury involving the oral commissures, uvula, and posterior pharyngeal wall. Mirror-assisted visualization and soft palate retraction using a Nelaton catheter optimize nasopharyngeal inspection during adenoidectomy. Additional hemostatic measures, including topical vasoconstrictors, gauze packing, warm saline irrigation, continuous suction, and suction coagulation, may reduce intraoperative bleeding while minimizing unnecessary thermal injury. CONCLUSIONS: Optimizing adenotonsillar surgery extends beyond the choice of surgical device. Simple, inexpensive, and reproducible technical modifications can substantially improve visualization, surgical exposure, hemostatic control, tissue preservation, and operative ergonomics, thereby contributing to safer, more standardized, and potentially more effective surgical procedures.

item.title: A senescence-driven fibroblast-macrophage feed-forward circuit promotes radiation induced cutaneous fibrosis.
item.dc:creator: Chung EJ, Kc S, Kwon S, White A, Chung JY, Jung Y, Ahn H, Zhang H, Cauley E, Citrin DE
item.description:
Authors: Chung EJ, Kc S, Kwon S, White A, Chung JY, Jung Y, Ahn H, Zhang H, Cauley E, Citrin DE
Journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics | DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrobp.2026.10.013
Published: 2026-Oct-24
PMID: 42925940



Abstract:
PURPOSE: Therapeutic radiation for superficial tumors may cause cutaneous fibrosis, a late side effect with limited treatment options. Here, we investigated the underlying mechanisms driving radiation-induced cutaneous fibrosis. METHODS AND MATERIALS: C3H/HeN mice received 35 Gy unilateral hind limb irradiation. Cutaneous tissues from irradiated and contralateral unirradiated legs were analyzed by spatial whole transcriptome profiling using the GeoMx Digital Spatial Profiler platform. Beginning at 5 weeks after irradiation, mice received the senolytic agent ABT-263 (50 mg/kg/day) or vehicle (n ≥ 10/group) by oral gavage (5 consecutive days followed by 2-week rest for 3 cycles). Hind limb contracture was assessed at 150 days after irradiation. Senescence and macrophage markers were evaluated by immunohistochemistry and quantitative PCR. Cellular senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors were evaluated in irradiated fibroblasts and their culture media using senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity assays and multiplex immunoassays. The senolytic activity of ABT-263 in irradiated primary fibroblasts and effects of ABT-263 on primary macrophage cultures were evaluated in vitro. RESULTS: Spatial whole-transcriptomic analysis of irradiated murine dermis identified expression patterns consistent with macrophage activation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-rich environment. In vitro studies identified that the irradiated fibroblast-derived SASP induced a senescent phenotype in unirradiated fibroblasts and macrophages. SASP-induced senescent-like macrophages acquired a CD206+ profibrotic phenotype and in concert with activated fibroblasts, initiated a feed-forward loop amplifying IL-6 and collagen production. SASP exposure increased expression of Bcl-2 family proteins in macrophages and fibroblasts, rendering both populations susceptible to clearance by the senolytic agent ABT-263. In vivo, ABT-263 effectively mitigated radiation-induced dermal fibrosis, depleted senescent fibroblasts and CD206⁺ macrophages, and reduced IL-6 expression CONCLUSION: Our findings identify senescence-driven reciprocal macrophage-fibroblast interactions as key mediators of cutaneous fibrosis and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of senolytic interventions for treating late radiation-induced skin injury.

item.title: Phase II Study of Neoadjuvant Cemiplimab for Stage II to IV Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Final Analysis.

item.description:
Authors: Gross ND, Miller DM, Khushalani NI, Divi V, Ruiz ES, Lipson EJ, Meier F, Su YB, Swiecicki PL, Atlas J, et al.

Abstract:
We previously reported the results of a multicenter phase II trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04154943) of neoadjuvant cemiplimab in resectable stage II to IV cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC), in which the pathologic complete response (pCR) rate was 51%. At the 19-month follow-up, estimated 12-month event-free survival (EFS) was 89%, with 11 EFS events. In this study, we report final EFS and overall survival (OS) at a median follow-up of 54 months. Overall, 16 EFS events occurred at final analysis. There were no new disease recurrence events. The five new EFS events were all comorbidity-related deaths without CSCC recurrence. item.title: Efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease (RISE UP): a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
item.dc:creator: Andemariam B, Kuo KHM, Algahtani FH, Al Kindi S, Ataga KI, Bartolucci P, Campbell A, Colombatti R, Glaros AK, Hafraoui K, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Andemariam B, Kuo KHM, Algahtani FH, Al Kindi S, Ataga KI, Bartolucci P, Campbell A, Colombatti R, Glaros AK, Hafraoui K, et al.
Journal: Lancet (London, England) | DOI: 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01480-7
Published: 2026-Oct-24
PMID: 42913682



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Persistent haemolytic anaemia and recurrent vaso-occlusion drive complications and accelerate mortality in sickle cell disease. Mitapivat, an oral allosteric activator of pyruvate kinase, increases ATP and decreases 2,3-DPG with the potential to improve haemolytic anaemia and reduce sickling. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease. METHODS: We report results from RISE UP, a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial from 69 sites across 15 countries. Patients older than 16 years with anaemia and recurrent sickle cell pain crises were randomly assigned (2:1) to either mitapivat 100 mg or placebo twice a day using permuted-block randomisation. Primary endpoints, assessed in all randomly assigned patients, were haemoglobin response (≥1·0 g/dL increase in average haemoglobin concentration from week 24 to week 52 compared with baseline) and annualised rate of sickle cell pain crises. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05031780, and the open-label extension is ongoing. FINDINGS: A total of 207 patients were randomly assigned to mitapivat (138 [67%]) or placebo (69 [33%]). 56 (41%) of 138 patients in the mitapivat group had a haemoglobin response, compared with two (3%) of 69 patients on placebo (adjusted difference 38%, 95% CI 29-47; two-sided p<0·0001). Serious adverse events were reported in 28 (20%) patients on mitapivat and 20 (29%) patients on placebo; one (1%) patient and 0 patients, respectively, were deemed treatment related. INTERPRETATION: Mitapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, with a novel mechanism that ameliorates haemolytic anaemia, has the potential to be an effective and convenient disease-modifying treatment for people with sickle cell disease. item.title: Modeling the survival impact of the Inflation Reduction Act out-of-pocket cap in multiple myeloma.
item.dc:creator: Zhao H, Teng S, Dong C, Meng Z, Tan Q, Wang R, Ji M, Schoen MW, Sanfilippo KM, Fiala MA, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Zhao H, Teng S, Dong C, Meng Z, Tan Q, Wang R, Ji M, Schoen MW, Sanfilippo KM, Fiala MA, et al.
Journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute | DOI: 10.1093/jnci/djag396
Published: 2026-Oct-23
PMID: 42924351



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral immunomodulatory imide drugs (IMiDs) have become standard of care for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM), but high out-of-pocket (OOP) costs may hinder treatment adherence. In 2025, the Inflation Reduction Act introduced a $2,000 annual OOP cost cap (IRAOOPcap) for Medicare Part D beneficiaries. In the absence of post-implementation data, we used comparative modeling to predict its survival impact. METHODS: The survival submodels of two independent Cancer Intervention and Surveillance Modeling Network (CISNET) natural history of multiple myeloma models were used. The models were parameterized using data from Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER)-Medicare, 2012-2021. We simulated survival among Medicare Part D beneficiaries with NDMM aged 66-75 and ≥76 years, under hypothetical scenarios shifting 0% (pre-IRAOOPcap) to 100% (best-case) of patients to IMiD use with high adherence and a realistic scenario using published data. We computed life-years gained (LYG) by comparing life expectancy (LE) under each scenario with that of the pre-IRAOOPcap scenario. RESULTS: Across models, the realistic/best-case scenario yielded LYG of 0.17-0.18/1.10-1.35 among patients aged 66-75 years, and 0.20-0.26/1.29-1.53 for those aged ≥76 years. These translated into 4,164-5,005/26,893-32,347 LYG at the population level for beneficiaries with NDMM in 2025. CONCLUSION: The IRAOOPcap may improve survival through increasing IMiD utilization and adherence among Medicare Part D beneficiaries with NDMM. The projected gains represent a meaningful proportion of contemporary survival for patients. Future research should validate these gains when real-world data are available and inform future policy adaptation and extension.

item.title: The Use of Combination Palliative Radiotherapy and Single-Agent Immunotherapy for the Management of Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) in the United Kingdom (UK).
item.dc:creator: Hurt C, Park S, Chambers J, Brammer C, Griffin M, Harilal V, Stone R, Haris PA, Shakir R, Karsera L, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Hurt C, Park S, Chambers J, Brammer C, Griffin M, Harilal V, Stone R, Haris PA, Shakir R, Karsera L, et al.

Published: 2026-Oct-23

Abstract:
Clinical data on combined Immunotherapy (IO) and palliative radiotherapy (RT) in HNSCC is scarce. HNSCC Palliative RT differs from curative intent RT as it does not involve elective nodal irradiation; therefore, an immune response may be more likely. We conducted a UK retrospective survey of patients starting palliative RT and IO monotherapy within 3 months of each other. About 75 patients were treated at 16 centres from January 2022 to December 31, 2023. About 89.3% received first-line Pembrolizumab and 10.7% second-line Nivolumab. 13.3% reported ≥ Grade 3 immune-related adverse events and 6.7% ≥ Grade 3 RTOG side effects; overall response rate (ORR) was 41.3%. Median overall survival (OS) was 10.2 months (95% CI: 6.5-16.2) and median progression-free survival (PFS) was 5.6 months (95% CI: 4.8-8.3). OS was significantly better in locally advanced disease non-amenable to radical treatment (OS HR = 0.42 (95% CI: 0.18-0.97), p = 0.043) and de-novo metastatic disease (OS HR = 0.35 (95% CI: 0.16-0.76), p = 0.008) compared to recurrent disease. Compared to starting IO > 6 weeks after radiotherapy initiation, OS was significantly better in those starting IO 0-6 weeks after radiotherapy initiation (OS HR = 0.40 (95% CI: 0.17-0.95), p = 0.037). The ORR in this cohort is higher than published data of single agent IO alone. Improved survival outcomes in patients receiving IO closer to RT with BED > 70 and alternative fractionation may reflect favourable patient selection but could be influenced by synergy between IO and RT. These findings are from non-randomised cohort data and should be seen as exploratory and hypothesis generating.

item.title: Microbeam radiotherapy - clinical and dosimetric investigation of a first clinical application.
item.dc:creator: Kraus KM, Day LR, Wilkens JJ, Combs SE, Bartzsch S
item.description:
Authors: Kraus KM, Day LR, Wilkens JJ, Combs SE, Bartzsch S
Journal: Radiation oncology (London, England) | DOI: 10.1186/s13014-026-02946-2
Published: 2026-Oct-23
PMID: 42920150



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microbeam Radiotherapy (MRT) is an emerging radiotherapy technique which delivers spatially fractionated beams on a micrometre scale. In preclinical studies MRT has demonstrated superior normal tissue sparing compared to conventional radiotherapy while maintaining tumour control. However, MRT has traditionally been achievable only at large synchrotron facilities which has impeded clinical translation. The development of a compact line-focus X-ray tube (LFXT) provides a pathway for clinical MRT, but identification of clinically and dosimetrically suitable patient scenarios is required for first-in-human trials. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Potentially eligible patients were selected from our patient cohort based on clinical criteria including palliative treatment indication, superficial tumour location, reproducible and safe positioning, minimal interference from other therapies, and expected benefit from MRT. Three-dimensional forward treatment planning was performed in Eclipse using gantry rotations, collimator positioning, and conformal masks to treat the clinical target volume (CTV). Dose was calculated in Eclipse using a custom Monte Carlo-based hybrid algorithm adapted for the compact LFXT system with a 300 kVp beam and an eccentric focal spot. A single-fraction equivalent uniform doses (EUD) of 3 Gy was prescribed to the target volume. Dose distributions were analysed using dose-volume histograms (DVHs), peak and valley depth dose profiles, and peak-to-valley dose ratios (PVDRs). RESULTS: Selected cases included primary lymphoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and superficial soft tissue metastases. Dosimetric analysis under exploratory assumptions demonstrated dosimetrically feasible treatment plans with optimal target coverage and organ-at-risk (OAR) sparing for gluteal, nuchal, and inguinal tumours. Maximum OAR doses remained below 8.5 Gy, except in bone or overlapping high-density regions. The mean peak and valley dose across all plans was 57.2 Gy and 3.9 Gy, respectively, with a mean PVDR of 15.4. Dose inhomogeneities were observed due to tissue heterogeneity, kilovoltage beam interactions, and a limited range of suitable gantry angles. Tumours in anatomically complex regions, including those in proximity to OARs or tissue inhomogeneities, showed less favourable trade-offs between target coverage and OAR sparing. CONCLUSION: This study identifies clinically and dosimetrically suitable scenarios for first-in-human MRT trials, highlighting superficial tumours as optimal initial indications. While peak, valley, and PVDR values align with preclinical evidence, their clinical significance remains uncertain. Careful, safety-driven dose escalation studies will be required to establish a foundation for responsible and effective clinical application of MRT in early-phase clinical trials.

item.description:
Authors: Livneh N, Wazana Y, Peled I, Carmel E, Peled C, Madgar O
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71014
Published: 2026-Oct-23

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether parent-captured oropharyngeal videos obtained using a handheld telemedicine device can assess tonsil size in children with sleep-disordered breathing compared with in-person clinical examination. METHODS: We conducted a prospective diagnostic accuracy study at a single tertiary pediatric referral center. A consecutive sample of 169 children scheduled for tonsillectomy, adenoidectomy, or adenotonsillectomy was enrolled. Parents obtained oropharyngeal videos using a handheld telemedicine device (TytoCare). Three blinded pediatric otolaryngologists independently graded tonsil size using the Brodsky scale. Interrater agreement, diagnostic performance relative to in-person examination, and video usability were assessed. RESULTS: Among 169 children (median age 4.4 years, IQR 3.3-7.6), 53% underwent adenotonsillectomy and 46% adenoidectomy alone. Interrater agreement for tonsil size grading was strong (Kendall's W = 0.88, p < 0.01) and remained substantial when grades were dichotomized as 0-2 versus 3-4 (Fleiss κ = 0.65, 95% CI: 0.58-0.73). Using the in-person examination as the reference standard, sensitivity was 70%, specificity was 86%, positive predictive value was 84%, and negative predictive value was 73%. Twenty-one videos (12%) were unusable by all evaluators and 54 (32%) by at least one evaluator, with higher rates in younger children. CONCLUSION: Parent-captured oropharyngeal videos may provide a feasible method for remote tonsil size assessment in selected children with sleep-disordered breathing. Strong interrater agreement and generally favorable parental attitudes support further evaluation of this approach, while additional validation is needed before routine reliance on video-based assessment for surgical decision-making.

Abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Improvements in head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment have increased survival rates, resulting in survivors living with side effects, such as head and neck lymphoedema (HNL). METHODS: We conducted an online, 51-item survey between February and October 2024. RESULTS: Participants included in the analysis of the (i) HNC healthcare professionals section (n = 73/113), and (ii) HNL therapists section (n = 40/46). 45% (n = 33/73) of the participants reported not having access to a specialized multidisciplinary team for HNL management. 55% (n = 22/40) of HNL therapists reported not having standardized institutional lymphoedema management protocols. Abstract:

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis. METHODS: REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting. FINDINGS: Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns. INTERPRETATION: Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis. FUNDING: Novartis.

item.title: Perioperative chemotherapy and stereotactic body radiotherapy versus perioperative chemotherapy alone in patients with high-risk, localised pancreatic cancer (MASTERPLAN): an open-label, phase 2, multicentre, randomised trial of the Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group.
item.dc:creator: Oar A, Kneebone A, Sjoquist KM, Espinoza D, Lee M, Le H, Gholamrezaei L, Chu J, Lynam J, Mallesara G, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Oar A, Kneebone A, Sjoquist KM, Espinoza D, Lee M, Le H, Gholamrezaei L, Chu J, Lynam J, Mallesara G, et al.
Journal: The Lancet. Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/S1470-2045(26)00532-2
Published: 2026-Oct-23
PMID: 42914998



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has poor outcomes and high rates of locoregional recurrence. MASTERPLAN evaluated whether stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) reduced locoregional recurrence in patients with high-risk, localised PDAC. METHODS: MASTERPLAN was an open-label, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted across 14 hospitals in Australia and New Zealand. Eligible participants were aged 18 years or older with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, and had previously untreated localised PDAC with at least one high-risk feature, including tumour size more than 4 cm, extrapancreatic extension, node-positive disease, borderline resectable disease, or locally advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1) using the method of minimisation to investigator-choice chemotherapy, with or without SBRT, stratified by participant cohort (potentially operable vs inoperable), planned chemotherapy regimen, randomisation before or within the first 28 days of chemotherapy, and institution. Chemotherapy consisted of mFOLFIRINOX (day 1 oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150 mg/m2, leucovorin 50 mg, and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 h every 14 days for six cycles; all intravenous) or gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days for three cycles; both intravenous). SBRT was delivered as 40 Gy in five fractions, with two to four fractions delivered per week, with real-time radiotherapy quality assurance. Surgical resection was considered following induction therapy, followed by a planned further 12 weeks of adjuvant chemotherapy with either mFOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine plus capecitabine (28-day cycles of 1000 mg/m2 intravenous gemcitabine administered on days 1, 8, and 15 with 830 mg/m2 oral capecitabine twice daily administered on days 1-21). Participants deemed not suitable for surgery continued the same chemotherapy for an additional 12 weeks with reassessment for surgical suitability permitted, for a total planned duration of chemotherapy of 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was 12-month locoregional recurrence in the intention-to-treat population, with safety endpoints analysed by treatment received. The trial planned to recruit 120 patients but due to slow accrual closed to recruitment early on Jan 6, 2025. Trial closure and database lock occurred on July 21, 2026. This trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trial Registry (ACTRN12619000409178) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04089150), and is complete. FINDINGS: Between Feb 26, 2020, and Jan 6, 2025, 74 participants (43 [58%] male, 31 [42%] female) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy and SBRT (n=49) or chemotherapy alone (n=25). After a median follow-up of 3·2 years (IQR 1·9-4·3), 12-month locoregional recurrence was 20·2% (95% CI 9·9-33·1) in the SBRT group and 52·0% (30·3-69·9) in the chemotherapy alone group (subdistribution hazard ratio 0·44 [95% CI 0·22-0·88]; p=0·022). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 33 (70%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group and 16 (64%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·27), with one (4%) treatment-related death secondary to biliary tract infection in the chemotherapy alone group. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were diarrhoea (seven [15%] in the SBRT group vs five [20%] in the chemotherapy alone group), and thromboembolic events (three [6%]) vs one [4%]). Overall grade 3 or higher serious adverse events occurred in 30 (64%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group, and 14 (56%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·24). There were two serious adverse events attributable to SBRT; grade 2 small bowel obstruction and grade 3 pancreatitis. INTERPRETATION: In patients with high-risk, localised PDAC, the addition of SBRT to chemotherapy was associated with significantly reduced locoregional recurrence without a significant increase in toxicity and warrants further investigation in larger studies. item.title: Head and neck cancer incidence and two-year mortality in Aotearoa New Zealand, 2009-2020: a national population-based cohort study.
item.dc:creator: Chauhan AS, Davie G, Barson D, Parackal SM, Russell-Camp T, Wong A
item.description:
Authors: Chauhan AS, Davie G, Barson D, Parackal SM, Russell-Camp T, Wong A
Journal: Cancer epidemiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.canep.2026.103264
Published: 2026-Oct-23
PMID: 42914788



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head and neck cancer (HNC) imposes a substantial burden in Aotearoa New Zealand (AoNZ), yet contemporary population-level data on incidence and early mortality across sociodemographic groups remain limited. METHODS: This population-based retrospective cohort study used New Zealand Cancer Registry to identify all primary HNC diagnoses from 2009 to 2020 (n = 6980). The cases were classified according to ICD-10 subsites. Incidence rates (IRs), age-standardised IRs, and age-standardised rate ratios were estimated by age, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic deprivation, and rurality. Regression models were used to estimate annual percentage change in IRs and to estimate adjusted risk ratios for two-year all-cause mortality. RESULTS: In total 6980 people were diagnosed with HNC; an overall incidence rate of 13.5 per 100,000 person-years (PY). Oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), the most common subsite, increased from 3.4 per 100,000 PY in 2009-2011-4.9 per 100,000 PY in 2018-2020, whereas IRs for oral cavity cancer (OCC), the second most common, were more stable. HNC IRs were higher among males, older adults, Māori, Pacific Peoples and people living in the most socioeconomically deprived areas, with subsite-specific differences: Māori experienced higher OPC incidence rates, while Pacific Peoples experienced higher OCC IRs. Within two years of diagnosis, 25.2% of patients had died. Two-year all-cause mortality was 44.4% for hypopharyngeal cancer, 30.9% for OCC, and 22.7% for OPC. Among people diagnosed with HNC, after adjusting for available sociodemographic factors and treatment timing, two-year all-cause mortality was higher for Māori, Pacific Peoples, and those in the most deprived quintile. Rurality showed no consistent association with incidence or two-year mortality. CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate an OPC-driven shift in HNC epidemiology in AoNZ and a persistent inequitable burden of both disease occurrence and early mortality, supporting stronger surveillance and equity-focused cancer-control responses.

item.title: Precancerous cervical lesions and associated factors among HIV-positive women in Southern and Eastern African countries: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.dc:creator: Alemu GG, Bazezew AM, Yirsaw AN, Wondie WT, Mengistie BA, Dagnaw TE, Aweke MN, Baykemagn ND, Lakew G, Gebretsadkan BT
item.description:
Authors: Alemu GG, Bazezew AM, Yirsaw AN, Wondie WT, Mengistie BA, Dagnaw TE, Aweke MN, Baykemagn ND, Lakew G, Gebretsadkan BT
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361185
Published: 2026-01-01

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women living with HIV (WLHIV) face a sixfold increased risk of cervical cancer compared to HIV-negative women. Most WLHIV residing in the Southern and Eastern African regions have a substantial HIV-related cervical cancer burden. Studies on precancerous cervical lesions (PCCL) and associated factors in WLHIV from these regions have inconsistent and inconclusive findings. Therefore, we aimed to synthesize the pooled prevalence of PCCL and associated factors among WLHIV in Southern and Eastern Africa. METHODS: This study was registered under PROSPERO (CRD420251123583) and conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 standards. Primary studies published from inception to 2025 in Southern and Eastern Africa were included. The methodological quality of studies was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa scale. Data extraction and statistical analyses were done in Microsoft Excel and STATA 17, respectively. Pooled prevalence, publication bias, subgroup, and sensitivity analysis were conducted. Associations were expressed as odds ratios (OR), and a p-value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: 44 studies met the inclusion criteria, with a sample size of 47,009. The pooled prevalence of PCCL was 22.25% (95% CI: 19.57, 24.93). Age at first sexual intercourse (< 18 years) (OR = 2.99, (2.34, 3.82)), multiparity (OR = 4.97, (3.21, 7.69)), having multiple sexual partners (OR = 3.06 (2.45, 3.83)), having a history of sexually transmitted infections (STI) (OR = 3.93 (3.23, 4.78)), smoking (OR = 7.01, (3.39, 14.49)), ever taking oral contraceptive pills (OR = 2.69, (1.85, 3.90)), low CD4 count (OR = 1.79, (1.56, 2.05)), and having not initiated antiretroviral therapy (ART) (OR = 2.02, (1.56, 2.62)) were significantly associated with an increased risk of PCCL. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS: The pooled prevalence of PCCL was high. Additionally, early first sexual intercourse, parity, STIs, multiple sexual partners, smoking, oral contraceptive use, CD4 count, and ART were positively associated with the occurrence of PCCL. Therefore, stakeholders shall implement interventions to avert future incidents of PCCL and address the identified factors.

item.title: Do community pharmacies unnecessarily recommend oral emergency contraception? A nationwide mystery caller investigation in Germany.
item.dc:creator: Langer B, Beck A, Dreier AM, Gabrieljan R, Hilgenhof H, Latuske J, Priepke C, Schaihadinow K, Schwarz H, Kunow C
item.description:
Authors: Langer B, Beck A, Dreier AM, Gabrieljan R, Hilgenhof H, Latuske J, Priepke C, Schaihadinow K, Schwarz H, Kunow C
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361027
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42912737



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Since 2015, oral emergency contraceptives (ECs) have been available in German community pharmacies without prescription as over-the-counter medicines. Given the financial burden, unnecessary hormonal exposure and associated side effects, systematic information gathering is crucial to prevent unnecessary recommendations. This study aimed to determine whether pharmacy staff ask the checklist questions recommended by the German Federal Chamber of Pharmacists (BAK) guideline and provide correct recommendations when oral EC is not indicated (appropriate outcome), and to examine associated factors. METHODS: A nationwide study using the simulated patient methodology - considered the "gold standard" - was conducted with a stratified random sample of 376 community pharmacies across Germany. Eight trained female mystery callers aged 21-24 simulated a scenario in which a combined oral contraceptive was forgotten once after sexual intercourse. However, the pill could still be taken within the 12-hour window, making oral EC unnecessary according to the BAK guideline. To ensure quality, each call was monitored by a second observer. RESULTS: Of 376 mystery calls conducted, 322 were included in the primary analysis. An appropriate outcome was achieved in 44.4% (143/322), while oral EC was unnecessarily recommended in 49.1% (158/322). The median questioning score was 2.0 of 4.0 points. A multivariable logistic regression model showed that a higher questioning score and mystery caller identity were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome. Qualitative findings indicated both positive counseling practices and notable deficiencies among pharmacy staff. CONCLUSION: The results show deficits in information gathering and appropriate recommendations. To improve counseling, the consistent use of the BAK checklist during telephone consultations should be explicitly recommended in the relevant guideline. Targeted training for pharmacy staff may help address professional and communication deficits. Surprisingly, some mystery callers were significantly associated with the appropriate outcome, highlighting the need for further research on the influence of vocal characteristics and last names in telephone consultations.

item.title: Pharmacokinetic diversity of baloxavir marboxil across rare avian species.
item.dc:creator: Shimazu Y, Obara RD, Miki M, Osaki H, Yoshimoto Y, Hayashi M, Toyoda K, Ozaki M, Hanada I, Matsumoto R, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Shimazu Y, Obara RD, Miki M, Osaki H, Yoshimoto Y, Hayashi M, Toyoda K, Ozaki M, Hanada I, Matsumoto R, et al.
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0361119
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42912701



Abstract:
High pathogenicity avian influenza virus (HPAIV) poses a serious threat to captive rare birds. Because effective countermeasures are limited, the use of human antiviral drugs to treat HPAIV infections in captive rare birds has been considered. Although the human antiviral drug, baloxavir marboxil (BXM), is not approved for the treatment of influenza virus infection in birds, previous studies demonstrated the antiviral efficacy of BXM in experimental avian models. Pharmacokinetic studies have also revealed substantial interspecies differences following BXM administration, suggesting the need to establish species-specific dosing regimens. In this study, BXM was administered to 14 avian species to optimize dosing regimens for each species. Oral administration of BXM using different methods revealed that drug-food interactions had a limited impact on systemic drug exposure. Pharmacokinetic analysis of BXM and its active metabolite, baloxavir acid (BXA), demonstrated marked interspecies variability in drug exposure, contributing to the development of optimized dosing regimens for each species. Furthermore, systemic exposure to BXA was strongly associated with drug absorption indicators, suggesting that species-specific differences in absorption efficiency largely determine BXA exposure among avian species. This study provides a pharmacokinetic basis for the rational use of BXM in diverse avian species. It contributes to the development of practical antiviral strategies to protect captive rare birds against HPAIVs.

item.title: Why Are We Doing Pediatric Parotid Surgery? Insights From a Tertiary Center's Experience.

Authors: Barham D, Brennan L, Stobbs N
Journal: The Laryngoscope | DOI: 10.1002/lary.71013
Published: 2026-Oct-22

Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To establish common clinicopathological themes of pediatric parotidectomy, aid decision making, and compare this to previously reported features and outcomes. METHODS: Retrospective cohort analysis of all pediatric parotidectomies over a 10-year period at a tertiary level pediatric hospital. RESULTS: Thirty-one patients were identified (15 male, 16 female) between the ages of 1 and 16. Primary parotid tumor was the most common reason for surgery (n = 15), followed by congenital abnormalities (n = 12). The most common histopathological diagnosis was acinic cell carcinoma (n = 6). The most common complication was temporary facial nerve weakness (29%). CONCLUSION: Primary parotid tumors were the most common reason for parotidectomy, and most of these were malignant. Of these, Acinic Cell Carcinoma was more prevalent than Mucoepidermoid Carcinoma. Pediatric parotidectomy is safe with a low permanent complication rate, but patients should be specifically counseled about temporary facial nerve weakness and the small risk of permanent injury.

item.title: Sexual dysfunction in men after radiotherapy for squamous cell carcinoma of the Anus: A danish anal cancer group DACG study.
item.dc:creator: Krogstrup MJ, Steffensen JH, Serup-Hansen E, Kronborg CJS, Spindler KG
item.description:
Authors: Krogstrup MJ, Steffensen JH, Serup-Hansen E, Kronborg CJS, Spindler KG
Journal: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.radonc.2026.111850
Published: 2026-Oct-22
PMID: 42913945



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sexual dysfunction, particularly erectile dysfunction (ED), is well documented after pelvic radiotherapy, but evidence in men with squamous cell carcinoma of the anus (SCCA) remains sparse. PURPOSE: To assess erectile and ejaculatory function, and sexual interest up to five years after curative-intent radiotherapy for SCCA, based on physician-graded toxicity and validated patient-reported outcomes (PROs). METHODS: This sub-study of the prospective DACG-I cohort (NCT05570279) included men treated with curative-intent radiotherapy for SCCA (2015-2020). PROs (EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-CR29) and physician-graded toxicity (CTCAE v4.0) were collected at baseline, 1, 3, and 5-years. Symptom prevalences were described descriptively. Longitudinal changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models on linearly transformed EORTC scores. RESULTS: Of 80 enrolled men, baseline data were available for 76. At baseline, majority were symptom-free. Erectile and ejaculatory dysfunction emerged mainly within 1-3 years after treatment and persisted through 5 years. For the total cohort, ejaculatory dysfunction increased from 4.5% at baseline to 12.3% at 3 years. Physician-assessed ED (NCI-CTCAE grade ≥ 2) increased from 11.9% to 39.3% at 3 years. PROs indicated greater deterioration in erectile function at parallel time points. EORTC scores confirmed moderate-to-major clinically important deterioration at 1 and 3 years. Sexual interest remained stable over time. CONCLUSION: Sexual dysfunction, particularly ED, represents an increasingly prevalent and persistent late adverse effect in men treated with curative-intent radiotherapy for SCCA. The early onset of symptoms and the limited extent of recovery underscore the need for structured assessment based on PROs to support timely identification and supportive care.

item.title: Consensus on current clinical workflow and future use of 3D models in parotid gland tumor surgery: A Delphi study.
item.dc:creator: Moll MCM, Karssemakers LHE, Braun LMM, van Alphen MJA, Valstar MH, Smeele LE, Zuur CL, Arends CR
item.description:
Authors: Moll MCM, Karssemakers LHE, Braun LMM, van Alphen MJA, Valstar MH, Smeele LE, Zuur CL, Arends CR
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108163
Published: 2026-Oct-22
PMID: 42913203



Abstract:
OBJECTIVE: MRI-based 3D models provide patient-specific spatial information on the relationship between parotid gland tumors and the facial nerve. However, their potential role in clinical practice and the level of support for their implementation remain unclear. This study aimed to assess the level of consensus among surgeons on the current clinical workflows in parotid gland surgery and the future role of 3D models. STUDY DESIGN: We used a three-round Delphi study to explore consensus among surgeons performing more than five parotid surgeries annually. Round 1 consisted of semi-structured interviews about parotid surgery, innovations, and the use of 3D models. Inductive analysis was used to formulate statements and questions for round 2. In rounds 2 and 3, participants rated the questions and statements on a 7-point adjective scale. RESULTS: A panel of 15 surgeons, including 9 otolaryngologists and 6 oral and maxillofacial surgeons from nine Dutch hospitals, completed all study rounds. Partial consensus was observed for 10% of statements in round 3. Trends toward greater importance of both MRI scanning and 3D model use were identified in cases involving malignancy, facial nerve dysfunction, deep lobe tumors, fixed tumors, non-palpable tumors, and indications for a mastoidectomy. Stronger trends toward importance were observed for using 3D models in preoperative planning and patient counseling than in their use during surgery. CONCLUSION: Although consensus was limited, this study identified indications for MRI use and highlighted the perceived value of 3D models in parotid gland tumor surgery.

item.title: The 5-mm margin in head and neck cancer surgery: From uncontrolled historical dogma to personalised surgery.
item.dc:creator: Roussel LM, Berghian A, Hapdey S, Clatot F
item.description:
Authors: Roussel LM, Berghian A, Hapdey S, Clatot F
Journal: Oral oncology | DOI: 10.1016/j.oraloncology.2026.108194
Published: 2026-Oct-22
PMID: 42913202



Abstract:
For decades, a histological margin of 5 mm has been used as the practical definition of a "clear" resection in Head and Neck squamous cell carcinoma, particularly in the oral cavity. This short communication revisits the origins of this threshold, ang argues that it is based more on historical convention than on true validation of oncological biology. Although retrospective studies and meta-analyses have reinforced the 5 mm rule, their interpretation is limited by treatment-selection bias since adjuvant radiotherapy was systematically delivered to patients whose margins fell below this value. Furthermore, the 5 mm definition does not consider how residual disease spreads. Available data suggest that front morphology, as determined by the worst pattern of invasion and tumour budding, is associated with the margin width, even though this needs to be confirmed prospectively. Rather than replacing margin distance, which remains clinically useful and validated, these factors could complement it. Integrating these factors into therapeutic decision-making could be a promising way to achieve personalised management.

item.title: Monthly high-dose cholecalciferol supplementation in prostate cancer patients (ProsD trial): A nested analysis of vitamin D metabolites, metabolic ratios, and biochemical safety.
item.dc:creator: Tan C, David MC, Anderson PH, Mason RS, Fraser DR, Kimlin MG, Sawyer RK, Amirmostofian M, Frydenberg M, Yaxley JW, et al.
item.description:
Authors: Tan C, David MC, Anderson PH, Mason RS, Fraser DR, Kimlin MG, Sawyer RK, Amirmostofian M, Frydenberg M, Yaxley JW, et al.
Journal: Cancer epidemiology | DOI: 10.1016/j.canep.2026.103258
Published: 2026-Oct-22

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effects of intermittent, high-dose cholecalciferol supplementation on circulating vitamin D metabolites and related biomarkers remain unclear. The ProsD randomised controlled trial evaluated the effects of monthly oral supplementation with 50,000 IU cholecalciferol in males with prostate cancer and assessed longitudinal changes in vitamin D metabolite responses. OBJECTIVE: To characterise vitamin D metabolites and ratios after a monthly dose of 50,000 IU cholecalciferol supplementation and to assess the effects on biochemical markers. METHODS: ProsD recruited and randomised 123 men with prostate cancer; 118 participants (placebo n = 40; vitamin D n = 78) provided blood samples at baseline, and from remaining participants at 0, 6, 12, and 24 months, at follow-up visits. Plasma vitamin D metabolites-25(OH)D3, 1,25(OH)2D3, 24,25(OH)2D3, and 3-epi-25(OH)D3-and vitamin D metabolite ratios (VMRs) were quantified. Longitudinal changes and between-group differences were evaluated using age-adjusted generalised estimating equations with estimated marginal means. Routine biochemical markers were also assessed. RESULTS: Compared with placebo, monthly cholecalciferol supplementation increased peak between-group difference at 24 months for 25(OH)D3 (+30.10 nmol/L; p < 0.01), 1,25(OH)2D3 (+12.44 pmol/L; p = 0.11), 24,25(OH)2D3 (+3.95 nmol/L; p < 0.01), and 3-epi-25(OH)D3 (+5.94 nmol/L; p < 0.01). The 25(OH)D3:24,25(OH)2D3 VMR increased in the placebo group but remained constant in the intervention group, and between-group analysis showed consistently lower ratios in the vitamin D group. All routine biomarkers remained within normal ranges throughout follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Monthly oral supplementation of 50,000 IU cholecalciferol in men with prostate cancer produced sustained increases across multiple vitamin D metabolites over 24 months, accompanied by adaptive shifts in metabolite ratios consistent with regulated catabolic activation, with no clinically meaningful abnormalities in biochemical markers. item.title: 630 nm light-emitting diode irradiation suppresses inflammation and promotes osteoblast differentiation in periodontal cell models - in vitro study.
item.dc:creator: Lee JK, Lee MS, Jeong JH, Ahn SH
item.description:
Authors: Lee JK, Lee MS, Jeong JH, Ahn SH
Journal: PloS one | DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0351995
Published: 2026-01-01
PMID: 42911963



Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Periodontal disease involves persistent inflammation and alveolar bone loss. Photobiomodulation using light-emitting diodes (LEDs) may regulate inflammation and bone remodelling, but the optimal wavelength and irradiation timing remain unclear. METHODS: Human gingival fibroblasts and RAW 264.7 macrophages were irradiated with 525, 630, or 850 nm LED light before or after lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation. The effects of 630 nm irradiation were further evaluated in primary mouse calvarial osteoblasts, MC3T3-E1 cells, bone marrow-derived macrophages, and RAW 264.7 osteoclast precursors. Inflammatory mediators, nitric oxide production, cell viability, osteoblast differentiation, and osteoclast formation were assessed. RESULTS: Among the wavelengths tested, 630 nm irradiation most consistently reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and secretion and decreased nitric oxide production without affecting cell viability. In primary osteoblasts and MC3T3-E1 cells, 630 nm irradiation at 5 and 10 J/cm² increased alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, osteogenic marker expression, RUNX2 protein levels, and Smad1/5/9 phosphorylation. In contrast, the same irradiation conditions did not significantly affect osteoclast differentiation or the expression of osteoclast-related markers. CONCLUSION: Irradiation with 630 nm LED light suppressed inflammatory responses and promoted osteoblast differentiation without enhancing osteoclastogenesis. These findings suggest that 630 nm photobiomodulation may provide a balanced therapeutic approach for periodontal disease, although further validation in animal models and clinical studies is required.

item.title: Sequential Therapy with Anlotinib and Radioiodine for Distant Metastatic Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: A Phase II Clinical Trial.

Abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radioiodine (RAI) alone exhibited limited efficacy in distant metastatic differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC). We hypothesized that pretreatment with anlotinib, a potent antiangiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitor, would reduce tumor burden and improve therapeutic response. METHODS: This prospective, single-arm phase II trial enrolled patients with measurable distant metastatic DTC. All patients received anlotinib 12 mg/day orally for 12 weeks. After confirmation of RAI-avid target lesions on diagnostic ¹³¹I-WBS, patients were treated with 7.4 GBq RAI and followed up for another 12 weeks. Sequential therapy continued until no effect of RAI could be anticipated. Primary endpoints were objective response rate (ORR) and safety. Registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2100045178; https://www.chictr.org.cn). RESULTS: 24 patients were enrolled. 14 (58%) were excluded due to non-RAI-avid target lesions; 10 (42%) with RAI-avid lesions received sequential therapy (median, 4.5 cycles). ORR was 60% (all partial responses), disease control rate 100%. With median follow-up 34.5 months, no disease progression or death occurred. In the subgroup of eight patients with bone target lesions, ORR was 50%. Grade 3 anlotinib-related adverse events occurred in 30% of patients; no grade 4/5 toxicities or grade ≥2 RAI-related events were observed. CONCLUSION: Sequential anlotinib followed by RAI therapy demonstrated promising antitumor activity (ORR 60%) and favorable safety in RAI-avid distant metastatic DTC, particularly in bone metastases. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in a randomized trial with an RAI monotherapy control arm.

item.title: Clinical Heterogeneity Across Oropharyngeal Cancer Datasets and Implications for Outcome Prediction.
item.dc:creator: Cabrera CI, Tamaki A, Koroukian SM, Love TE, Singer ME, Teknos TN, Rezaee R, Zhang L
item.description:
Authors: Cabrera CI, Tamaki A, Koroukian SM, Love TE, Singer ME, Teknos TN, Rezaee R, Zhang L
Journal: JAMA otolaryngology-- head & neck surgery | DOI: 10.1001/jamaoto.2026.3290
Published: 2026-Oct-22
PMID: 42911606



Abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Multi-institutional oropharyngeal cancer datasets are increasingly used for research, yet systematic evaluation of data completeness and its clinical impact remains limited. Unrecognized institutional heterogeneity in variable availability, coding conventions, and patient characteristics can introduce substantial bias into combined analyses. OBJECTIVE: To systematically characterize data availability patterns and clinical heterogeneity across 2 major oropharyngeal cancer datasets, evaluate their impact on survival, and develop evidence-based recommendations for multi-institutional research design. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A cross-sectional analysis and retrospective cohort study was conducted of the RADCURE dataset (2005-2017) from Princess Margaret Cancer Centre (Toronto, Canada) and the HNSCC-Oropharyngeal dataset (2005-2012) from MD Anderson Cancer Center (Houston, Texas). Patients with complete data on patient and disease characteristics were included. Data were analyzed from 2023 to 2026. EXPOSURES: Institutional dataset, human papillomavirus (HPV) status, tumor (T) stage, node (N) stage, harmonized treatment modality, smoking status, and age at diagnosis. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Data completeness rates across clinical and end point variables; overall survival assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis with Peto-Peto weighted log-rank tests, restricted mean survival time, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression stratified by HPV status; machine learning discrimination and calibration for 1-, 5-, and 10-year survival prediction. RESULTS: The final analytic cohort comprised 1972 participants (median [IQR] age, 59.5 [53.4-67.0] years; 347 female [17.6%] and 1625 male [82.4%] individuals), 1482 from the RADCURE and 490 from the HNSCC-Oropharyngeal datasets. Of the total, 1263 had HPV-positive disease (64.0%). Substantial institutional differences were observed across demographic characteristics, HPV distribution, and treatment modality. After comprehensive adjustment, the hazard ratio for treating institutions was 1.19 (95% CI, 0.93-1.52), not excluding a clinically meaningful effect. HPV status violated the proportional hazards assumption, and its prognostic effect was quantified using restricted mean survival time, demonstrating a clinically meaningful survival advantage for patients with HPV-positive disease in both datasets. Machine learning ensemble models achieved moderate to good discrimination (1-year area under the curve [AUC], 0.820; 5-year AUC, 0.777; 10-year AUC 0.786) with institution consistently ranking as a low-importance predictor. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional analysis and cohort study, multi-institutional oropharyngeal cancer datasets exhibited substantial heterogeneity requiring systematic harmonization prior to combined analyses. Systematic harmonization and rigorous assumption testing should be prerequisites for multi-institutional oropharyngeal cancer analyses; after appropriate adjustment, treating institution did not independently predict survival.
